new_roles.company: Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care
new_roles.title: APP Medical Director, Quality & Safety
new_roles.description:
**Help shape the clinical future of one of the region's most respected healthcare organizations.**

Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care is seeking an experienced Advanced Practice Provider leader to serve as **APP Medical Director, Quality & Safety**.

The Medical Director reports to the Chief Medical Officer and provides direct leadership to an assigned group of providers and Lead Providers, while holding network-wide responsibility for clinical quality standards, quality surveillance, patient safety, and performance improvement across Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care. This senior leadership position combines meaningful clinical practice with the opportunity to advance evidence-based care and strengthen clinical performance across a growing network in Connecticut and New York.

**Why Join Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care?**

* Regional leadership opportunity with impact across urgent care centers throughout Connecticut and New York.
* Partnership with an experienced and collaborative medical leadership team.
* Ability to influence clinical quality, safety, and provider performance at scale.
* Opportunity to mentor providers and develop future clinical leaders.
* Strong operational infrastructure and organizational support.
* Continued clinical practice while serving in a senior leadership role.
* Proudly affiliated with Yale New Haven Health.

**A Regional Leadership Opportunity**

Working collaboratively with the Chief Medical Officer, fellow Medical Directors, Lead Providers, and operational leaders, the APP Medical Director, Quality & Safety will translate clinical performance data, quality findings, and emerging risks into meaningful improvements in care delivery, provider performance, and patient outcomes.

**What You'll Do**

* Provide direct leadership, performance management, coaching, and professional development for an assigned group of Advanced Practice Providers.
* Directly supervise and develop assigned Lead Providers, supporting their effectiveness in provider oversight, clinical escalation, and quality improvement.
* Lead network-wide clinical quality and patient safety initiatives, including quality surveillance, clinical event review, clinical risk identification, and performance improvement.

* Establish and oversee chart review, documentation integrity, coding accuracy, and provider feedback processes, ensuring findings translate into appropriate corrective actions and measurable improvements in clinical care.

* Develop and monitor evidence-based clinical standards, including diagnostic testing, clinically significant results follow-up, referral and escalation processes, and adherence to established clinical protocols.

* Partner with the Chief Medical Officer and operational leadership on clinical governance, regulatory readiness, and risk mitigation.

* Maintain meaningful clinical practice while serving in a leadership capacity.

**What Success Looks Like**

A successful leader in this role will:

* Demonstrate measurable improvements in clinical quality, patient safety, and provider performance across the urgent care network.

* Develop and support high-performing providers and Lead Providers through effective coaching, accountability, and professional development.

* Use clinical performance data, chart review findings, and quality metrics to identify opportunities, implement improvements, and sustain results.

* Foster consistent, evidence-based care and a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement across geographically diverse teams.

* Champion a patient-centered approach to urgent care that supports timely access, appropriate clinical management, and seamless coordination across the Yale New Haven Health delivery network.

**Qualifications**

* Current unrestricted PA or APRN licensure and appropriate board certification.
* Significant urgent care clinical experience with expertise managing the broad range of acute illnesses, injuries, and procedures encountered in urgent care practice.
* Substantial clinical leadership experience, including direct provider supervision, performance management, accountability for clinical quality and patient safety outcomes, and successful implementation of measurable clinical improvement initiatives.
* Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills across multidisciplinary teams.
* Experience leading across multiple clinical sites and utilizing quality and performance data to drive improvement strongly preferred.
* Ability to travel throughout the region as needed to support providers, quality initiatives, and operational priorities.

**Working Arrangement**

* This is a regional, multi-site leadership position supporting Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care locations throughout Connecticut and New York. The position is not assigned to a single clinical site and requires travel throughout the network.
* Clinical Commitment: 0.3 FTE.
* Medical Leadership Responsibilities: 0.7 FTE.

**Ready to Take the Next Step?**

If you're an accomplished Advanced Practice Provider with a passion for clinical leadership, quality improvement, and patient safety, we invite you to explore this opportunity to make a meaningful impact across the Yale New Haven Health Urgent Care network.

**Apply today to learn more.**

new_roles.title: Director Quality
new_roles.description:
**SUMMARY:**

Reporting to the President, C.E.O., Directs and coordinates activities of personnel at all Hutchinson Sealing Systems facilities engaged in Quality Management System to prevent or eliminate defects in new or existing products or process by performing the following duties personally or through subordinates. This position is designated as a sensitive function for quality, engineering, manufacturing, supplier, audit, compliance, and operational information, including quality performance data, customer requirements, product and process development information, audit findings, corrective actions, supplier performance records, and proprietary company information. The incumbent is responsible for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets in accordance with company policies and customer requirements.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

* Analyzes, evaluates, and presents information concerning factors such as quality performance, production capabilities, manufacturing problems, customer quality trends, and quality planning of new products for consideration by other members of the management team.
* Presents and evaluates alternative methods and procedures to establish standardized quality systems based on best practices.
* Participates with other top management personnel in formulating and establishing company policies, operating procedures, and goals.
* Participates in review of product development activities and APQP milestones.
* Conducts Quality System Management review meetings with top management to assess performance and compliance to customer quality requirements.
* Reviews technical problems and procedures of departments and recommends solutions to problems or changes in procedures.
* Confers with engineers and managers about quality assurance of new products and process to improve manufacturing capability.
* Reviews technical publications, articles, and abstracts to stay abreast of technical and quality system developments in industry.
* Travel required on a frequent basis to suppliers and customer facilities as well as other Hutchinson facilities.
* Provides internal quality system audit of Hutchinson Sealing Systems locations.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

Master's degree (M.A.) or equivalent; or four to ten years’ related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Qualifications may be waived by management. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:**

None.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Manages subordinates in department. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of this unit. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complains and resolving problems.

**TEAM SKILLS:**

Hutchinson is built around teamwork. This position requires the use of good team skills such as cooperation, information sharing, task sharing, timely completion of assignments, good listening and communication skills and overall respect for other team members.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:**

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret common scientific and technical journals, financial reports, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community. Ability to write speeches and articles for publication that conform to prescribed style and format. Ability to effectively present information to top management, public groups and/or boards of directors.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:**

Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference, and fundamentals of plane and solid geometry and trigonometry. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

**COMPUTER SKILLS:**

Ability to use word processing, spreadsheet applications. Must be familiar with internet research, Microsoft Office software, and the use of e-mail.

**REASONING ABILITY:**

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close, vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

**HEALTH AND SAFETY:**

Must actively support our Health Safety and Environmental policy, immediately report all Safety hazards and correct them when able to safely do so, participate in all required Safety Training, meetings, inspects, and use all required PPE.

 

We are 40 000 men and women who meet the challenges faced by our automotive, aviation, defence and industry customers every day. Our passion for challenge and our enthusiasm encourage us to imagine, design and produce high performance and innovative fluid, sealing system and anti-vibration solutions. Working at Hutchinson means being curious about everything, contributing to the evolution of mobility and reducing carbon emissions.

 

Join us and show what drives you!

 

A French company with an international presence (25 countries): 170 years of history and passing on our know-how.

5 billion in turnover, with 5% invested in R&D.

new_roles.title: Head of Quality
new_roles.description:
**About Bora:**

Bora Biologics is a global biologics CDMO delivering integrated development and GMP manufacturing solutions from First‑in‑Human through licensed commercial supply. While many CDMOs are structured primarily for early clinical programs, Bora Biologics is purpose‑built for commercialization. Our inspection‑proven, bi‑coastal U.S. manufacturing platform and integrated development center provide the infrastructure, regulatory discipline, and operational precision required for sustained global market supply.

**Summary**

Reporting to the VP, Regional Head of Quality, the BBUL Site Head of Quality is responsible for developing, implementing, and overseeing a comprehensive Quality Management strategy aligned with corporate policies, client expectations, and global regulatory requirements. This role ensures products from development through commercialization are safe, effective, and fully compliant with applicable CGMP/GxP standards. As a key member of the site leadership team, the Director/Sr. Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for the Quality organization, which includes Quality Assurance and Quality Control. The role partners cross-functionally with all departments to foster a strong culture of quality, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement while ensuring regulatory compliance and client satisfaction. The Director/Sr. Director also directs day-to-day quality operations, drives operational excellence and process optimization, supports execution of strategic and tactical initiatives, and ensures timely resolution of quality and compliance issues to maintain business performance and inspection readiness.

 

**Essential Functions**

*Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

* P rovide strategic leadership and overall accountability for the site Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with global policies, procedures, CGMP/GxP standards, and applicable regulatory requirements across the U.S. and international markets including EU.
* Partner with the Site Leadership Team (SLT) to strengthen and sustain a proactive culture of quality, escalating significant compliance risks and driving timely, effective resolution of quality issues.
* Lead and oversee regulatory inspections and audits, ensuring inspection readiness, effective agency interactions, and timely, compliant responses to observations.
* Direct all core Quality functions, including batch record review, material and product disposition, deviations and change control, document control, QC, QA oversight of all GMP functions including validation, operations, and facility activities.
* Provide leadership to ensure uninterrupted support for successful product transfers through robust quality oversight and operational excellence.
* Serve as the senior Quality leader supporting development initiatives and phased clinical programs, ensuring appropriate compliance throughout product development activities.
* Lead the Quality organization in achieving operational and strategic objectives, including budget planning and management, workforce planning, project execution, and organizational effectiveness.
* Establish and monitor key quality metrics (e.g., deviations, CAPAs, change controls, product release) to foster accountability. Evaluate system effectiveness and drive corrective action.
* Oversee quality indicators and operational efficiencies, implementing action plans to mitigate risks and streamline quality processes.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing Quality organization that operates as a trusted, collaborative business partner, while driving talent development, succession planning, and employee growth.
* Establish clear, consistent, and effective communication across the Quality organization and with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure alignment on priorities, risks, and business objectives.
Perform additional responsibilities and strategic initiatives as assigned 

*The above statements are intended to describe the nature of work performed by those in this job and are not an exhaustive list of all duties. Nothing in this job description restricts managements right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time which reflects management’s assignment of essential functions.*

**Minimum Education, Experience and Skills**

Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or a related area of study

**Experience:**

* At minumum15 years of pharmaceutical industry experience with at least 10 years of Quality experience, both QC and QA in biopharma/biotech in a CGMP pharmaceutical manufacturing environment with early and late-stage products.
* 5+ years of senior leadership experience driving Quality strategy, compliance initiatives, continuous improvement and staff development.
* Extensive experience developing, implementing and improving quality systems directly related to biologics drug substance manufacturing CGMP
* Proven track record of successfully managing and leading regulatory inspections, audits, and remediation activities with global health authorities with demonstrated success in leading a company through cGMP pre-approval and post-approval inspections.
* Proven ability to build and sustain a transparent, collaborative, and quality-focused culture that promotes accountability, engagement, and operational performance.
* Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing organizational change within complex regulated environments.
* Demonstrated ability to develop staff at all levels.
Experience with developing and managing budgets. 

**Skills and Abilities**

* Strong working knowledge of global regulatory requirements and quality standards, including US FDA, EMA, PIC/S, and ICH guidelines.
* Demonstrated success in leading organizations through sound decision-making, strategic problem-solving, and effective communication at all levels of the business.
* Prior experience within a CDMO environment is strongly preferred
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and communicate complex quality and compliance matters clearly and effectively.
* Proven ability to lead, mentor, and support teams through crisis management, organizational transformation, cultural change, and business growth initiatives.
* Highly adaptable and resilient, with the ability to perform effectively in fast-paced, high-pressure environments while maintaining focus on priorities and outcomes.
* Strong leadership capability with a demonstrated ability to empower teams, identify high-potential talent, and drive employee development and succession planning.
* Results-oriented leader with strong analytical and problem-solving skills focused on continuous improvement and operational excellence.
* Skilled at building trusted relationships and collaborating effectively with cross-functional peers, senior leadership, clients, and regulatory agencies.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in biological or chemical sciences
* Experience with US FDA, China FDA, Health Canada, EMEA, PMDA, and ANVISA is preferred
* Knowledge of and experience with GLP and/or GCP regulatory inspections a plus
Strong operational excellence experience or qualification 

Base Salary Range 192000-270000

 
 

**Compensation and Benefits**

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees’ wellbeing, including:

* Competitive salary and performance-based incentives
* Comprehensive health coverage including medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Retirement savings plans with employer matching contributions
* Paid time off
* Professional development opportunities
* Employee wellness programs and resources
* Employee Assistance Program and Mental Health Resources

**Core Values**

*At Bora, our values guide everything we do — from how we solve challenges to how we support our people. We lead with a solutions-first mindset, strive to do the right thing, stay proactive, and above all, respect everyone.*

Bora Pharmaceuticals is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all applicants and employees according to all applicable equal opportunity and affirmative action laws, directives and regulations of federal, state and local governing bodies and agencies. In keeping with this commitment, Bora Pharmaceuticals will recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles, without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex (including factors related to pregnancy or child birth), national origin, age, marital status, familial status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity status with regard to public assistance, employment status, local human rights commission activity, status as a protected veteran, genetic information, atypical hereditary cellular or blood trait, or any other protected category.

new_roles.description:
About Us:

Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the hard work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.

**Production**

From sourcing raw materials to manufacturing, order placement, pricing and quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results -driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.

Specific Responsibilities Would Include:

Centric Brands is looking for a dynamic, creative and resourceful Vice President of Production, Soft Accessories, to join its team. This individual must be a self-starter and collaborative leader who takes initiative, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and is excited to accelerate transformation across Centric Brands. The Vice President of Production, Soft Accessories, oversees all facets of global development, manufacturing and supply chain operations for cold weather accessories, including scarves, gloves, hats, beanies and related knit accessories. new_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
***Ready to lead a function, not just a shift? This is your next step.***

American Armor Gloves makes high-quality nitrile gloves here at home in South Carolina. Healthcare workers, first responders, and essential workers across the country rely on what we build. Our purpose is simple: **We strengthen America by building quality protection at home.**

We're a lean, growing manufacturer scaling toward 320–350 people, and we've spent the past year building the foundation for that growth: a redesigned organization, a clear vision with quarterly milestones, defined leadership roles, and a new leadership and compensation architecture. Manufacturing is the heart of that growth, and we need a leader ready to own it.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The Director of Manufacturing is one of the most essential roles in our company. You'll own the end-to-end performance of our Manufacturing department, turning business plans into consistent, safe, high-quality production results.

This role is built for an accomplished Manufacturing Manager who is ready to take the next step. You've proven you can run a strong operation. Now you're ready to **lead through systems and leaders rather than personal effort on the floor**, and to build a manufacturing function that performs at a high level no matter which team is on shift.

Reporting to our VP of Operations, you'll be the bridge between enterprise strategy and shift-by-shift execution. You'll set the systems, build the leaders, and own the results.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* **Own manufacturing performance.** Deliver results across safety, quality, OEE, throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, scrap, and downtime through accountable leaders and strong systems.

* **Build repeatable production systems.** Design shift handoffs, accountability routines, labor deployment standards, and scheduling so performance never depends on heroics.

* **Lead and develop your Shift Manager team.** Coach your Shift Managers as leaders, not only as production operators, and build the next generation of manufacturing leadership.

* **Integrate compounding and batching.** Keep material availability, formulation compliance, and production demand aligned and well governed.

* **Drive continuous improvement.** Lead projects that reduce waste, improve workflow, raise OEE, and close performance gaps, in partnership with Process Engineering.

* **Partner across the business.** Work side by side with Quality, Process Engineering, Maintenance, Logistics, and People & Culture to remove barriers to production.

* **Build workforce capability.** Own training plans, manufacturing career pathways, and engagement so our workforce is ready to support growth.

**WHAT YOU'LL OWN**

You'll set daily and weekly production priorities, deploy labor across shifts, manage Shift Manager performance, and direct improvement projects within manufacturing. You'll shape manufacturing KPI targets, capacity planning, equipment needs, and staffing structure through your recommendations to the VP of Operations. You'll lead Shift Managers, Production Planning, and Batching/Compounding leadership, with a frontline team of Production Supervisors and Manufacturing Associates across multiple shifts.

**A REAL CAREER PATHWAY**

We grow leaders deliberately, and this role is designed as a launch point, not a ceiling. Our leadership framework defines exactly what it takes to grow from functional leadership into executive leadership, and we invest in getting high performers there.

* **Where you go next.** The Director of Manufacturing is a direct pathway to VP of Operations or other senior operations leadership, based on demonstrated enterprise judgment, cross-functional partnership, and the strength of the leadership bench you build.

* **How you get there.** Expect direct mentoring from the VP of Operations, exposure to enterprise planning and capital decisions, cross-functional visibility, and formal leadership development.

* **A clear standard.** Your growth is measured against the same competency framework used for job descriptions, performance reviews, and succession planning, so you always know where you stand and what comes next.

* **Visibility at the top.** Our annual bench-strength review puts strong leaders on the executive team’s radar early.

**WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW**

* **Essential to the mission.** Every glove we ship runs through the function you lead.

* **Build, not just run.** Our organization is lean and still forming, so you'll shape systems and standards that scale with the business.

* **A clear operating rhythm.** A shared vision, quarterly milestones, and a common scorecard keep leaders aligned and connect your work to company priorities.

* **Leave a legacy.** You'll develop Shift Managers into future Directors and Supervisors into future Shift Managers, building a team that carries the company forward.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Industrial Technology, Business, or a related field, or equivalent progressive leadership experience

* 8–10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership in a high-volume environment

* Proven success leading multiple shifts and developing frontline leaders

* A track record of owning department performance through KPIs, systems, and accountable leadership

* Strong cross-functional partnership with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and HR

* Solid knowledge of OSHA safety requirements and manufacturing quality systems

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, ERP/MRP systems (NetSuite preferred), KPI dashboards, production scheduling, and QMS

**Bonus points for:** experience in medical device, PPE, chemical processing, or FDA-regulated manufacturing; Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement practice; ERP implementation; and leading through growth and scale.

**HOW YOU LEAD**

You lead safely, every shift, not only when incidents happen. You hold leaders accountable through systems, not by stepping in for them. When something breaks, you fix the system, not just the shift. You raise problems early and directly. You treat Quality, Engineering, and Maintenance as partners, and you understand how manufacturing affects the entire business.

**READY FOR YOUR NEXT STEP?**

If you're a Manufacturing Manager ready to own a function, build leaders, and grow into enterprise leadership with a company that's scaling with purpose, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today.

*American Armor Gloves is an equal employment opportunity employer and does not discriminate against employees or job applicants on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, mental or physical disability of a qualified individual, veteran or military status, pregnancy, marital status, familial status, genetic information, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state or local law.*

new_roles.title: Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
Bold Thinking. World Changing. At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
Explore what’s possible. Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
Step into the future. SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
Are you bold thinking? Find your place on our team and help us change the world!
 
 
**Primary Objective:** 
Join an innovative semiconductor manufacturing organization at the forefront of advanced technology and manufacturing excellence. The Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing owns the operational, financial, and strategic leadership of the Bloomington fabrication facility, including the Advanced Technology Services (ATS) Process Engineering Technician team. This role ensures the factory achieves world-class safety, quality, output, cycle time, and cost performance while directing a 24/7 organization and partnering across engineering, planning, and quality teams to meet all customer and business commitments.
 
In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, strategic planning, budgetary ownership, and leadership to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient semiconductor manufacturing. You will be responsible for driving absolute excellence across safety, quality, output, cost optimization, and ensuring smooth production flow to consistently meet internal and external customer quality and on-time delivery (OTD) commitments, and fab velocity metrics / key performance indicators (KPIs).
 
The successful candidate will own the organizational design and talent strategy for their organization, serving as a role model and lead a highly matrixed organization consisting of the Manufacturing team, Process Engineering Technicians group, and Flow Engineers. This role is expected to partner closely with Program Managers, Technical Leads, Wafer Planning, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development teams to improve operational performance, resolve manufacturing constraints, and deliver business objectives. This leader will play a critical role in transforming factory capabilities to meet strict customer commitments and flexible demand by influencing long-range capacity and setting standards for the MN fab operations organization.
 
 
**Major Areas of Accountability:** 

* Operations Leadership: Lead the daily and long-term operational execution in the fab, as well as the ATS technician and flow engineer teams to meet all production starts, output targets, yield expectations, cycle time goals, and quality standards, including setting clear priorities for the organization. Direct, develop, and coach the 24/7 operations teams—including Production, ATS Process Engineering Technicians, and Flow Engineers—to ensure capability, accountability, and organizational readiness.
* Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and empower the Production team, Process Engineering Technicians and Flow Engineers to provide effective manufacturing support, maintain production continuity, and resolve process and workflow issues
* Budgetary Responsibility: Own the fab operating budget, including labor, materials, maintenance, and operational spending; drive cost-reduction initiatives and evaluate capital investments using ROI-based decision-making.

* Manufacturing Performance: Partner with Industrial Engineers, and drive continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, WIP management, yield, quality, equipment availability, and manufacturing cost using data-driven decision-making and structured problem-solving.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development to resolve production constraints, improve equipment readiness, and maintain stable manufacturing operations.

Responsible for the organizational design and talent strategy of these teams, with a focus on cultivating and retaining key talent, developing future leaders and preparing current leaders for the next level role.

**Required Qualifications:** 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related technical discipline.
* Experience: Minimum 12 years in semiconductor manufacturing or operations; minimum 5+ years leading fab operations in a senior manager or director capacity within a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
* Skills:
* Demonstrated ability to improve manufacturing performance (throughput, cycle time, yield, cost, and customer delivery).
* Expertise in wafer planning, WIP management, or production scheduling.
* Strong capability in statistical process control (SPC), structured problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making.
* Demonstrated leadership with large technical teams, with an ability to communicate and collaborate cross-functionally, delivering results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of managing a 24/7 manufacturing organization and guiding cross-functional teams through technical tool or yield crises.
* Citizenship: US Citizen required.

**Physical Requirements:** 

* Ability to enter the cleanroom in full PPE to provide technical and operational support.
* Ability to navigate multi-level fab environments, including prolonged walking and standing when needed.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

* Education: Master’s or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
* Experience: Deep knowledge of advanced Complimentary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) nodes, fab toolsets (Lithography, Etch, Diffusion, Thin Films, Chemical Mechanical Polish, Metrology, Metals), and factory automation systems.

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Sourcing
new_roles.description:
**Job Description:**
====================

NOTE: This role is based in New York City and encourages a minimum of two days per week in the SoHo office. Some roles or teams may require additional in-office attendance if the essential functions of the role require it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Strategic Sourcing is a key global leadership role responsible for the strategic sourcing, manufacturing, commercialization, and production execution of Scholastic's merchandise portfolio supporting Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade Publishing, Discovery Fairs, and future consumer product initiatives.

Reporting directly to the SVP Manufacturing who is responsible for Global Supply Chain and Procurement, this position serves as the critical bridge between Product Development, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Publishing, and global manufacturing partners.

This leader partners with internal stakeholders from the earliest stages of product ideation, providing expertise in product engineering, sourcing strategy, manufacturing capabilities, material selection, cost optimization, and production feasibility. The objective is to transform creative concepts into high-quality, innovative products that deliver exceptional customer experiences while achieving aggressive cost, quality, and speed-to-market objectives.

The role oversees a global sourcing portfolio exceeding $200 million annually and leads an international team of approximately 12 professionals located across the United States and India. The position may be based in the United States, China, or India and requires extensive collaboration with domestic and international suppliers and manufacturing partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

**Product Development, Ideation & Publishing Partnership**

* Serve as a strategic partner to Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade, and other stakeholders to translate creative concepts and intellectual property into compelling, manufacturable products.
* Engage early in product ideation, bringing manufacturing and sourcing expertise to decisions around materials, formats, construction, packaging, features, price points, and production methods.
* Proactively introduce new product concepts, materials, manufacturing capabilities, and supplier innovations that expand Scholastic's product opportunities.
* Partner throughout the development cycle from concept, specification, prototyping, sampling, and costing through pproval and production.
* Challenge and improve concepts where appropriate to enhance consumer appeal, quality, manufacturability, sustainability, speed, and cost.

**Consumer Products & Sourcing Strategy**

* Lead development of the sourcing and manufacturing strategy supporting Scholastic's expanding consumer-products and merchandise initiatives.
* Partner with business and publishing leadership to identify new product categories and opportunities across Book Fairs, Discovery Fairs, retail, e-commerce, licensing, and other emerging channels.
* Develop category sourcing strategies addressing manufacturing regions, supplier capabilities, cost, lead times, minimum quantities, tooling, quality, and supply-chain risk.
* Build a proactive pipeline of product ideas and manufacturing capabilities that can be regularly presented to internal stakeholders.
* Maintain awareness of consumer trends, emerging categories, materials, and manufacturing technologies and translate those insights into actionable product opportunities.

**Global Vendor Development & Innovation**

* Proactively identify and develop innovative manufacturers and product-development partners, particularly those offering engineering expertise, rapid prototyping, unique materials, creative capabilities, and new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop suppliers that can function as extensions of Scholastic's product-development organization, proactively bringing forward new concepts and capabilities.
* Continuously evaluate the supplier portfolio to improve competitiveness, increase speed, diversify supply, reduce risk, and enable entry into new categories.

**Global Sourcing, Cost & Operational Leadership**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive global sourcing strategy supporting more than $200 million in annual product expense.
* Establish sourcing roadmaps and supplier-diversification strategies that anticipate future business requirements and reduce dependency on individual suppliers or regions.
* Ensure products consistently meet expectations for quality, safety, regulatory compliance, sustainability, cost, and on-time delivery.

**Supplier Engagement & Global Travel**

* Maintain direct senior-level engagement with strategic manufacturing partners and regularly visit supplier facilities to evaluate capabilities, innovation, quality, capacity, and operational performance.
* Significant international travel is expected, with consistent travel to Asia, particularly China and India, as well as other global sourcing markets as required.
* Use supplier visits as product-development and innovation opportunities to identify new materials, manufacturing processes, capabilities, and product concepts for Scholastic.
* Participate in relevant trade shows, sourcing events, and supplier innovation sessions to identify emerging capabilities and potential partners.

**Organizational Leadership**

* Lead and develop a global organization of approximately 12 professionals across the United States and India.
* Build a culture combining sourcing discipline with creativity, product knowledge, commercial thinking, and an entrepreneurial approach to product development.
* Develop team capabilities in product ideation, product development, supplier innovation, value engineering, and strategic sourcing.
* Build strong partnerships across Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and senior leadership, positioning the organization as a strategic product-development partner.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success will be measured through product development and innovation, cost per unit and total landed-cost, speed to market, supplier innovation and diversification, quality and compliance, on-time performance.

**About Scholastic**

For more than 100 years, Scholastic Corporation (NASDAQ: SCHL) has been meeting children where they are – at school, at home and in their communities – by creating quality content and experiences, all beginning with literacy. Scholastic delivers stories, characters, and learning moments that empower all kids to become lifelong readers and learners through bestselling children’s books, literacy- and knowledge-building resources for schools including classroom magazines, and award-winning, entertaining children's media. As the world's largest publisher and distributor of children's books through school-based book clubs and book fairs, classroom libraries, school and public libraries, retail, and online, and with a global reach into more than 135 countries, Scholastic encourages the personal and intellectual growth of all children, while nurturing a lifelong relationship with reading, themselves, and the world around them. Learn more at www.scholastic.com.

Some benefits that we offer:

 

* Full suite of health and wellness benefits (including a $0 deductible Medical Plan)
* Retirement Savings Plan 401(k) with options for both Roth and Traditional Contributions
* Tuition-Free programs for undergraduate and graduate degrees
* Generous Parental Leave Program
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with opportunity for discounted stock at a 15% discount

Thank you for your consideration in choosing Scholastic.

HOW YOU CAN FIT **(Qualifications)**

A minimum of 10 years of experience as a valued member of a non-book/novelty/ merchandise development team. Proven track record working at a well established company representing a diverse product catalog consisting of products attractive to consumer interest and educationaly directed.

Comfort in travel globally and managing teams remotely and developing deep relationships with vendors in China and India along with others Asian regions.

Direct book experience and knowledge of the book publishing cycles and development timelines.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Description:

**Join Weiss-Aug – A Leader in Precision Manufacturing and Innovation**

Be part of a company that’s shaping the future of manufacturing where your ideas, skills, and passion matter.

Weiss-Aug, is a leading provider of advanced manufacturing and engineering solutions with advanced facilities across the U.S. and Mexico for over 50 years.

**Why Join Us?**

At Weiss-Aug we are driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement. As a recognized leader in the industrial and commercial sectors, specializing in high-volume metal stamping, thermoplastic molding, and value-added assembly solutions for the medical, aerospace & defense, automotive, interconnect, telecommunications and consumer goods industries, we take pride in cultivating a collaborative and forward-thinking work environment.

We're currently seeking a passionate and skilled ***Director of Operations*** to join our team and contribute to our mission of delivering high-quality, engineered solutions to our customers worldwide. In this role you will be responsible for planning and directing line management and related manufacturing support activities including manufacturing floor inspection, manufacturing engineering, materials management and safety/environmental engineering. Establishes and implements manufacturing policies, controls and procedures to further the company's interest in efficiently producing quality products. Contributes to achievement of sales objectives and to the establishment. Prepares or assists in the annual budgets for all departments and is responsible for profit and loss of the division. Manages Manufacturing Managers of Molding and Stamping, Purchasing, Warehouse, Manufacturing Engineering, Customer Service/Planning.

**Responsibilities**

* Management of manufacturing operations. Plans, schedules, organizes, and staffs manufacturing and manufacturing support functions. Assures that all groups within manufacturing organization are properly staffed and coordinated; and that personnel in each group are properly qualified, directed and trained to perform their duties effectively.
* Interprets company sales forecasts and shop orders and establishes accurate manufacturing plans to assure that our customers' requirements are met, that is, defect free product on time.
* Coordinates with Engineering, Sales and new product development engineering to maintain an awareness of current and future product plans.
* Develops and manages material control, manufacturing control, production scheduling, and planning systems to assure achievement of output schedules which will meet company sales requirements.
* Maintains material and parts inventories which are adequate to ensure the fulfillment of production schedules with minimum inventory expense.
* Plans and develops manufacturing facilities and equipment for efficient production of products.
* Works with tooling/engineering to investigate product quality and manufacturing problems and determine the most cost-efficient solutions.
* Develops and assists with the annual budget of all departments; develops and is responsible for all standard costs. Recommends pricing based on the profit objective of the company. Is responsible for the profit and loss of the division.
* Meets or exceeds all TQM measurements as agreed upon annually.
* Is a member of the executive team and steering team which are responsible for the development of company policies and plans.
* Participates with other top managers in the development of company business policies as needed.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree Mechanical or Industrial Engineering.
* 8-10 years precision manufacturing experience including some experience in molding. (10 years in management role).
* Strong leadership skills.
* Should have a working knowledge of computerized manufacturing systems.

This position is at our ***East Hanover, NJ*** location.

Pay Range: $150,000 - $180,000

**Other Benefits Include**

* Medical, Dental and Vision
* 401 (k) with company match
* Holiday, Vacation and Sick Time
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Health Savings Accounts (HSA)
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Cigna Wellness Incentive Program
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Short Term Disability
* Group Life and Accidental Insurance
* Sun Life – Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
* Smoking Cessation Program
* Pet Insurance

**US Pay Transparency**

The base salary for this role will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, experience, and internal consistency.

If your salary requirements exceed the advertised range and you remain interested in Weiss-Aug, we encourage you to apply.

Weiss-Aug is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. Applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristics protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Location:

Garden City, NY, US, 11530

Business Unit: Treitler FMH

Posting Date: Nov 20, 2026

Job Description:

**Position Summary:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for leading Hughes-Treitler operations to achieve business objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and customer satisfaction. This hands-on leadership role provides strategic and day-to-day direction for manufacturing, materials, and operational excellence while ensuring the organization has the talent, capacity, processes, and resources required to support current demand and business growth. The Director establishes operating plans, drives accountability, builds organizational capability, and leads continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance, expand capacity, control costs, and strengthen customer responsiveness.

 
 

**Supervisory Responsibilties:**

The position has direct reports but must be able to work in partnership with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Production in support of the departmental objectives. 



**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Lead and develop Operations teams to effectively support day-to-day execution, strategic business objectives, customer requirements, and growth plans.
* Establish operating strategies, objectives, budgets, capital requirements, material plans, labor requirements, and organizational priorities aligned with customer and business needs.
* Ensure the organization is structured and staffed with the talent, resources, and capabilities needed to meet customer quality, technical, delivery, and turnaround-time expectations.
* Partner with business leadership to achieve key performance indicators, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, throughput, backlog reduction, customer lead time, productivity, labor utilization, cost, and profitability.
* Lead the development and execution of the site Lean and Operational Excellence roadmap, using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, TPM, SIOP and daily management practices to improve flow, yield, cycle time, productivity, and cost performance.
* Establish and monitor operating standards, performance metrics, and management routines that drive accountability, timely problem-solving, and sustained results.
* Drive capacity planning and expansion initiatives, including capital equipment, automation, facility, tooling, staffing, and process investments required to support business growth.
* Manage operating expenses and capital investments in accordance with approved budgets; identify and execute cost-reduction and productivity opportunities.
* Ensure effective planning and control of materials, inventory, suppliers, production schedules, and labor resources to support quality, cost, and delivery commitments.
* Collaborate with Quality, Engineering, Sales, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to resolve operational issues, support new product introductions, strengthen manufacturability, and meet customer requirements.
* Provide leadership for robust root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and customer performance.
* Participate in the development and execution of the business strategy and translate strategic priorities into actionable operating plans and measurable objectives.
* Support commercial and customer-facing activities, including operational reviews, pricing and capacity analyses, customer visits, and performance presentations.
* Recruit, develop, coach, and retain operations talent through performance management, career development, succession planning, cross-training, and ongoing capability building.
* Foster a culture of accountability, employee engagement, collaboration, innovation, safety, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* Author annual performance reviews and develop continuing education and advancement paths for entire department.
* Demonstrate the ability and willingness to use AI tools appropriately to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and cost performance, including identifying suitable use cases and critically evaluating AI-generated outputs.
 

**Required Skills and Abilities:**

* Strong leadership, project management, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations and continuous improvement initiatives in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Proficiency with Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, Kaizen, TPM, and other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to establish performance metrics, analyze operating data, prioritize competing demands, and drive accountability for results.
* Proven ability to lead change, manage multiple complex initiatives, and meet critical deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Exceptional interpersonal, written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to build effective work relationships.
* Strong customer orientation and demonstrated ability to balance customer requirements with operational, financial, and organizational priorities.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, exercise sound judgment, and maintain a hands-on leadership presence across the operation.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning and manufacturing systems; experience with SIOP or related planning processes preferred.
* Demonstrated history of successful change management and implementation of operational excellence improvements.
* Strong interpersonal, leadership and organizational skills and the ability to communicate with all levels of the organization from the production floor to the executive office.
* Willingness to work a flexible schedule and travel as needed to support business requirements.
 

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or another related technical discipline required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience in a low-volume/high-mix, build-to-order, or engineered-products environment; experience in aerospace, defense, metal-forming, precision machining, brazing, welding, or another highly regulated industry preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading salaried and hourly employees.
* Demonstrated experience leading Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, and continuous improvement programs with measurable results.
* Demonstrated experience driving operational planning, capital and capacity expansion, production and materials management, cost optimization, organizational improvements, and customer-facing operational reviews.

**Other**

* Due to the nature of Hughes-Treitler's programs and products, applicants must have the legal right to work in the US and additionally must be legally authorized to access export-controlled information and source code.

**Physical Requirements:**

* None

**Compensation**
----------------

Employee Type: Salaried

Currency: USD

Salary Minimum: 200,000

Salary Maximum: 225,000

Incentive: No

Disclaimer: Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.

new_roles.title: Director, Global Supply Chain Center of Excellence – Chemical Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**The Opportunity:**
--------------------

**Position purpose**

 
 

Lead the global Supply Chain Center of Excellence across three pillars: Planning Excellence & Governance; Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement; and Data, Systems & Digital Enablement.

 
 

Strengthen supply chain performance by establishing consistent planning practices, delivering actionable analysis and measurable improvements, and enabling reliable data and effective planning technology. Partner with regional supply chain leaders to build capabilities and sustain improvements while regional teams retain operational supply and inventory accountability.

 
 

**How you will thrive and create an impact**

 

**Planning Excellence & Governance**

* Establish global planning standards, business rules, decision rights, and exception thresholds.
* Define planning horizons, freeze rules, and handoffs between master supply planning, site scheduling, materials planning, and regional supply planning.
* Own S&OE/S&OP process design, calendars, review standards, and escalation methods.
* Establish Plan for Every Part (PFEP) standards and review methods for finished goods, raw materials, and packaging.
* Assess planning-process adoption and effectiveness, identify gaps, and lead improvements with regional owners.
* Build planner capabilities through training, coaching, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

**Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement**

* Establish common KPIs, dashboards, and performance-analysis methods across regions.
* Lead capacity scenarios and inventory modeling to support supply, working-capital, and investment decisions.
* Develop inventory policies, safety-stock methods, and replenishment recommendations with regional teams.
* Partner with Manufacturing and regional planning teams to improve capacity utilization, campaign planning, and planning parameters.
* Identify and quantify value leakage, including excess inventory, expiry, write-offs, premium freight, and avoidable expediting.
* Develop prioritized improvement initiatives with clear business cases, accountable execution owners, and milestones.
* Track corrective actions and validate realized benefits with Finance, distinguishing recurring savings, cash release, and cost avoidance.

**Data, Systems & Digital Enablement**

* Establish master-data standards, business ownership, validation controls, and data-quality remediation processes.
* Prioritize SAP planning gaps and configuration issues and lead business resolution with IT.
* Lead the business workstream for planning system implementation and SAP integration, including requirements, data readiness, testing, and deployment readiness.
* Advance reporting and workflow automation to improve planning productivity and exception management.
* Develop AI-enabled reporting, exception insights, and commentary with appropriate validation and accountable business review.
* Lead planner training, system adoption, and post-implementation improvement.
* Maintain a technology roadmap aligned with planning needs and measurable business outcomes.

**Leadership and cross-functional alignment**

* Set a balanced CoE roadmap across the three pillars, prioritizing resources against business needs.
* Lead and develop the CoE team with clear responsibilities and performance expectations.
* Partner with regional supply chain leaders, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Quality, Finance, and IT to implement improvements.
* Communicate progress, risks, benefits, and decisions required to supply chain leadership.
 

 

**Measures of success**

 
 

**Planning excellence**

* Adoption and effectiveness of planning standards, PFEP reviews, and S&OE/S&OP processes.
* Improved planning discipline, handoffs, and planner capability.

**Analytics and improvement**

* Quality and use of analysis in business decisions.
* Inventory and capacity improvements delivered with regional teams.
* Reduction in value leakage and Finance-validated benefits.

**Data and digital enablement**

* Planning-data accuracy and closure of critical data issues.
* Delivery and adoption of SAP, Netstock, and automation improvements.
* Measurable improvements in planning productivity and decision support.
 

 

**What we're looking for**

 
 

**Required**

* Typically 10 or more years of progressive supply chain experience, including team leadership and cross-functional improvement.
* Strong knowledge of master planning, capacity planning, inventory management, PFEP, and S&OE/S&OP.
* Demonstrated experience establishing planning governance and delivering measurable operational improvements.
* Proven leadership of teams and large, complex transformation programs across multiple sites or regions.
* Strong track record leading planning-system implementations, organizational change, training, and sustained adoption.
* Deep SAP planning expertise, including master-data governance and configuration, sufficient to guide business design and challenge technical solutions.
* Strong analytical judgment, with experience directing BI reporting, dashboards, and optimization initiatives to improve business performance.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, establish planning governance, and deliver measurable operational and financial results.

 

**Preferred**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Chemicals or batch/process manufacturing experience.
* Experience leading a global-scale CoE or planning transformation.
* SAP and Netstock or comparable planning-platform experience.
* ASCM/APICS certification, Lean Six Sigma qualification, or an advanced degree.

They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position. new_roles.title: Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53229
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations owns cross-suite production performance across upstream and downstream operations in both single-use and stainless-steel suites. As the site scales to six suites, this leader is accountable for delivery of the site production plan, manufacturing cost performance, and workforce strategy, drives daily operational discipline through MDI and lean standard work, and represents manufacturing on the site Leadership Team.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own cross-suite production performance and site-wide annual batch plan attainment across all operating suites

* Lead fully integrated, operations-focused suite teams, with upstream, downstream, and support activities managed within each suite, and clear day-to-day accountability for execution, staffing, and scheduling

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary responsible party for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Champion adoption of lean principles across manufacturing including standardized work, visual controls, and a culture of continuous improvement (kaizen) as the site scales to six suites

* Lead the production plan across all suites, working with supply chain to align the supply plan to the production schedule through the site S&OP process

* Drive the site's daily MFG MDI process at the suite level surfacing, escalating, and resolving issues in real time across all shifts

* Serve as the manufacturing process and cost owner, driving cost-per-batch performance and contributing to the site Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget

* Manage workforce strategy and ramp for the manufacturing organization, including multi-shift staffing, hiring, training, and qualification of operators as new suites come online

* Ensure cGMP compliance, right-first-time execution, and inspection readiness on the manufacturing floor, partnering closely with Quality on deviations and batch record performance

* Champion a zero-harm EHS culture and drive manufacturing safety performance across all shifts

* Lead manufacturing operational readiness for suites entering service, partnering with Technical Services on tech transfer, process readiness, and PPQ execution

* Build and maintain a lean, scalable manufacturing organization, including area management and round-the-clock shift coverage within each suite

* Partner with quality, technical services, supply chain, environmental health & safety, and operational excellence to resolve issues quickly and operate as one aligned site leadership team

* Establish high standards for performance management and accountability; develop and retain talent; perform other duties as required

* Own a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance
 

 

**This role requires****:**

* B.S in engineering, life sciences, or a related technical field
 + Sr. Director: 15+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Executive Director: 18+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Level will be determined based on experience
* Financially literate, with demonstrated experience of delivering production plan attainment, managing cost per batch, and operating within an annual budget

* Experience leading the start-up and ramp of manufacturing suites or facilities

* Experience leading large, multi-shift GMP organizations and building leadership depth

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

 
 

As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

 
 

For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.

 
 

**Salary Range (annually)**

$207,000.00 - $407,400.00
