existing_roles.description:
Apogee Architectural Metals
  
  
Apogee Enterprises, Inc. (NASDAQ: APOG), founded in 1949 and headquartered in Minneapolis, MN designs and delivers architectural products and services that enclose and enhance commercial buildings. www.apog.com
  
  
Apogee Architectural Metals is a segment of Apogee specializing in aluminum framing, windows, storefront, curtainwall, and entrance systems. We provide integrated capabilities, including design, engineering, extrusion, finishing, fabrication and assembly, across North America. Through our brands including Alumicor, EFCO, Linetec, Tubelite, and Wausau, we deliver quality, consistency, and value-added services throughout our portfolio.
  
  
**Position Summary**
The Director, Quality is a senior quality leader accountable for transforming quality performance, capability, and culture across the business. Reporting to the VP, Operations, this leader will set the quality agenda, lead the Quality organization, and establish the operating discipline, systems, and leadership routines required to deliver consistent customer and operational outcomes. This role requires a proven quality leader who can move beyond compliance to build a scalable quality operating model, elevate accountability across sites, and influence leaders at all levels to adopt new standards, behaviors, and ways of working.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Set and execute the quality strategy, operating model, governance routines, and performance expectations needed to improve quality outcomes across sites
* Lead, coach, and develop Quality Managers and site quality teams to strengthen capability, accountability, decision-making, and execution discipline
* Build a scalable quality operating system that integrates QMS standards, metrics, technology, problem solving, and leadership routines into daily operations
* Use customer feedback, quality data, audit findings, and operational trends to identify systemic issues, prioritize action, and eliminate recurring failure modes
* Partner with the VP, Operations, site leaders, and functional leaders to align quality priorities with operational performance, customer commitments, and business objectives
* Lead significant customer, product, process, or operational quality issues with clear escalation, root-cause discipline, corrective action, and organizational learning
* Lead quality transformation initiatives that reduce variation, improve process capability, strengthen operating discipline, and deliver measurable customer and business impact
* Influence leaders across operations, engineering, supply chain, commercial, and functional teams to remove barriers and adopt new standards, behaviors, and ways of working
* Report quality performance, transformation progress, risks, recommendations, and business impact to the VP, Operations and senior leadership
* Develop and maintain enterprise-wide Quality Management Systems (QMS), ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, customer, and company standards.
* Lead supplier quality strategies, including qualification, performance management, audits, and corrective action processes to ensure consistent raw material and supplier performance.
* Ensure data integrity and leverage digital quality tools, analytics, and technology solutions to improve visibility, decision-making, and process control.
* Own customer quality performance, including complaint management, warranty reduction initiatives, customer audits, and key customer quality relationships.

**Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities**

* Strong quality leadership with the ability to connect quality strategy, operational execution, customer outcomes, and business performance
* Ability to lead managers and teams while influencing cross-functional leaders in a matrixed, multi-site organization
* Strong communication and change leadership skills, including creating clarity, building commitment, managing resistance, and sustaining adoption
* Enterprise mindset with the ability to challenge current-state practices, address systemic issues, and raise the standard for quality performance
* Talent builder and operating leader who can align resources, develop people, and deliver measurable results through others

**Education And Experience**

* Education

+ Bachelor's degree in Quality Management, Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred

* Experience

+ 10+ years of progressive quality, operations, or manufacturing leadership experience, including accountability for quality strategy, performance, systems, governance, and standards
+ Experience leading quality managers and teams in a complex, multi-site manufacturing environment
+ Proven success transforming quality systems, operating discipline, metrics, governance, and leadership routines
+ Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders, lead enterprise-level change, and drive adoption across functions, teams, and sites
+ Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) Development and Implementation Experience. Experience in TQMS (Total quality management system; this is more driven and aligned with our AMS and Lean CI activities). This also help to target few key organizations I like to target. Supplier Quality Management and Audit Programs Management. Policy Development and Deployment Experience preferred to form a strategy and deploy/implementation.

**Work Environment/Travel Requirements**

* Frequent exposure to manufacturing environment
* Overnight travel requirements will be variable based on projects and business activities, expected up to 50% depending on home location
* Physical Requirements

+ Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments.
+ Lift up to 10 lbs.

*This job description outlines the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified.*
**Our Benefits**
We care about and invest in our employees. We are proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support their well-being and foster professional development. Here is a glimpse of what you can look forward to if you join our team.
  
  

* Competitive Benefits Package for employees and their dependents (Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, Disability)
* Incentive Plans
* 401(k) with employer contribution and match
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan with employer match
* Paid Time Off (Vacation and Sick Time)
* Paid Holidays
* Tuition Reimbursement Program
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Wellness Program
* Training and Career Progression

Apogee and our brands are an Equal Opportunity Employer.

**Working Location: Tennessee, Bartlett**
**Workplace Flexibility: Onsite**
**For more than 100 years, Olympus has focused on making people’s lives healthier, safer and more fulfilling.**
Every day, we live by our philosophy, True to Life, by advancing medical technologies and elevating the standard of patient care so people everywhere can fulfill their desires, dreams, and lives.
  
  
Our five Core Values empower us to achieve Our Purpose:
  
  
**Patient Focus, Integrity, Innovation, Impact and Empathy.**
Learn more about Life at Olympus: https://www.olympusamerica.com/careers .
  
  
**Job Description**
The Director of Quality, Barlett Operations is responsible for cGMP Operations of the facility inclusive of manufacturing quality, repair quality, distribution quality, quality inspection and quality systems. This role will ensure quality systems and processes are established, maintained, and continuously improved to consistently deliver right first-time quality, safeguard patient safety, and ensure customer satisfaction. The Director of Quality will ensure that the site is inspection ready at all times, manage and facilitate site audits and inspections, lead execution of commitments to regulators, and ensure that quality and/or compliance issues are corrected in a timely manner. This role will lead site initiatives aimed at building and sustaining a strong culture of quality and will work collaboratively with other functions at the site to achieve quality and business objectives. This position is the default Quality Management Representative for the Bartlett campus and reports dotted line to Top Management at the Bartlett campus.
  
  
**Job Duties**

* Leadership of the Site Quality organization and serves as site quality management representative ensuring efficient and flawless execution of quality systems and processes to ensure product quality and compliance with global and site policies and procedures, FDA regulations, and other applicable regulations, standards and guidance.
* In accordance with established budget, builds organizational capability and capacity to meet both the current and future needs of the business through talent acquisition, employee training / development and performance management.
* Directs activities to ensure that the site is in a continued state of compliance and inspection readiness including analysis and evaluation of data and presentation to senior management to ensure that projects are appropriately prioritized in alignment with regulatory requirements and business goals.
* Hosts external regulatory inspections and audits and ensures successful outcomes through inspection readiness activities, inspection management and observations resolution.
* Promotes awareness of regulatory requirements and expectations and ensures understanding of quality system requirements across the site. Identifies site training needs and leads efforts to ensure effective training delivery.
* In accordance with quality system and technical requirements and risk management documents, ensures implementation of effective process controls for manufacturing, servicing and supply chain operations that support timely delivery of products that consistently conform to their specifications. This includes validation and maintenance of the Site Master Validation Plan, calibration, equipment maintenance, critical component evaluations, and quality inspections.
* Anticipates and identifies quality and compliance risks and proactively collaborates with Operations and Supply Chain leaders to identify potential areas of process and product variability.
* Implements controls to prevent escape of nonconforming product, drives timely and thorough root cause investigations for quality issues (e.g., NCs, customer complaints), and ensures implementation of effective corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to mitigate recurrence of quality problems. Acts with appropriate levels of urgency commensurate with risk and escalates issues to management.
* Lead complex investigations to identify causes of problems to safeguard patient safety and business continuity.
* Utilizes data to assess the overall health and effectiveness of the site’s quality system and processes and identifies areas to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
* Maintains budgetary oversight for the Site Quality Operations organization. Partners with Finance and Operations business partners to ensure that expenses, headcount and capital are in alignment with business goals, financial targets and strategic plans.
* Partners closely with the site leadership team to prioritize programs to reduce product failures and ensures timely execution of initiatives.
* Engage in a positive manner with team members from all disciplines to enhance the culture of quality and maintain a patient and customer focused quality mindset.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Job Qualifications**
**Required:**

* BA/BS degree or equivalent experience in a Life Science, Engineering, or Physical Science. Advanced technical degree and/or MBA preferred. Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certification desired.
* A minimum of 10 years of cGMP experience in quality management (with direct shop floor experience) within the MedTech industry.
* Experience with durable medical devices, and a strong understanding of repair operations and servicing requirements to ensure they continue to meet safety and performance specifications over their usable life.
* Demonstrated experience influencing senior level management and key stakeholders and leveraging cross-functional partnerships for successful execution of critical quality initiatives.
* Experience interpreting and applying business requirements and regulations (FDA and other applicable global authorities) into sustainable quality processes leveraging industry best practices.
* Proactive approach to quality and compliance, with a focus on innovation and adaptation in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong ability to think and act globally, be fearless change agent while managing risks, develop future visions and engage audiences to drive transformation.
* Capable of presenting clear and insightful thoughts based in facts and data gain trust, build confidence and to influence key stakeholders across the business.
* Persistence to continuously improve, never settling for status quo, while keeping customer satisfaction and customer value central.
* Must be a self-starter with high personal accountability and courage to always do the right thing.
* Driving cultural change in a complex and diverse Olympus organization.
* Will work with global teams, availability will include working across global time zones.

**Why join Olympus?**
We offer a holistic employee experience supporting personal and professional well-being through meaningful work, equitable offerings, and a connected culture.
  
  
**Equitable Offerings you can count on:**

* Competitive salaries, annual bonus and 401(k)\* with company match
* Comprehensive medical, dental, vision coverage effective on start date
* 24/7 Employee Assistance Program
* Free live and on-demand Wellbeing Programs
* Generous Paid Vacation and Sick Time
* Paid Parental Leave and Adoption Assistance\*
* 12 Paid Holidays
* On-Site Child Daycare, Café, Fitness Center\*\*

**Connected Culture you can embrace:**

* Work-life integrated culture that supports an employee centric mindset
* Offers onsite, hybrid and field work environments
* Paid volunteering and charitable donation/match programs
* Employee Resource Groups
* Dedicated Training Resources and Learning & Development Programs
* Paid Educational Assistance

* Center Valley, PA and Westborough, MA

For more than 100 years, Olympus has pursued a goal of contributing to society by producing products designed with the purpose of delivering optimal outcomes for its customers around the world.

existing_roles.description:
**Position Overview:**

The Director of Quality will lead the quality function across the organization and create the operating model required for the company’s next stage of growth. This leader will be accountable for enterprise quality strategy, product and process quality, supplier and customer quality, and the effectiveness of the company’s quality management systems. The role will maintain applicable certifications, including ISO 13485, ISO 9001, and AS9100, while establishing a disciplined approach to quality diligence and integration for future acquisitions.

The Director of Quality must combine independent judgment with a practical understanding of manufacturing. This leader will know what strong quality looks like, but will build it in a way that fits the company's scale, products, customers, and maturity. Success requires the ability to move between enterprise strategy and a specific customer or production issue; challenge legacy practices while respecting operational knowledge; and bring people through change with clarity, evidence, and follow-through.

This is not a quality-systems-only position. The Director must remain close to manufacturing, customers, and the issues that affect product conformity, delivery, cost, and trust. The successful candidate will bring the rigor expected in regulated manufacturing, apply it without unnecessary bureaucracy, and build a quality organization that can identify risk early, solve problems at their source, and support sustainable growth.

**Essential Functions:**

* Set the global quality strategy. Assess the company's current quality environment and establish a multiyear roadmap aligned with business strategy, customer commitments, regulatory obligations, and acquisition plans. Translate the roadmap into clear priorities, resources, ownership, and measures of success.
* Lead the quality organization. Direct and develop quality leaders and teams across the sites. Define the structure, capabilities, decision rights, and functional accountability required to support a larger international manufacturing organization.
* Own the enterprise quality management system. Ensure effective governance and execution across document and change control, training, nonconformance, CAPA, complaints, risk management, supplier controls, internal audits, management review, and other core processes. Maintain applicable certifications and compliance with customer and regulatory requirements.
* Strengthen product and process quality. Partner with Operations and Engineering to improve quality planning, process validation and control, inspection, calibration, measurement systems, first-article or new-product readiness, and change execution. Use disciplined problem solving and prevention to reduce defects, scrap, rework, escapes, and recurring failures.
* Lead customer and supplier quality. Establish consistent expectations for customer issue response, supplier qualification and monitoring, supplier corrective action, and escalation. Ensure material issues are contained quickly, investigated to root cause, resolved with effective corrective action, and communicated with credibility.
* Create audit and inspection readiness. Lead the enterprise internal audit program and oversee registrar, customer, and regulatory audits. Maintain visibility to findings, commitments, certification status, and systemic risk, and verify that corrective actions are timely and effective.
* Use data to govern performance. Establish a focused set of enterprise and site quality measures, including customer complaints, defects, escapes, scrap and rework, supplier performance, CAPA effectiveness, and audit performance. Lead global management review and give executives a clear view of trends, risk, and required actions.
* Harmonize with purpose. Define the policies, standards, escalation requirements, and controls that must be common across the organization. Rationalize legacy processes and quality technologies, including eQMS capabilities, while preserving local differences that are justified by product, customer, regulatory, or operating needs.
* Lead quality through acquisitions. Support quality due diligence by assessing systems, certifications, audit history, customer and regulatory commitments, product and process risk, and organizational capability. Build and execute risk-based integration plans with clear Day 1 controls, remediation priorities, and a realistic path to the quality model.
* Exercise independent quality authority. Ensure that Quality has direct access to the information and leaders needed to escalate material risk. Maintain clear authority to contain nonconforming product and stop release or shipment when applicable requirements may not be met, while building shared ownership of quality across the business.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, quality, or a related technical field.
* At least 10 years of progressive quality experience in manufacturing, including at least five years leading quality teams or leaders.
* Demonstrated success leading quality across multiple manufacturing sites, business units, or regions.
* Experience with product and process quality, quality engineering, customer quality, supplier quality, and quality management systems in a regulated or highly technical environment.
* Strong working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 9001, and AS9100, including direct responsibility for audits, certification, corrective action, and management review. Equivalent experience spanning multiple regulated standards will be considered.
* Deep experience with CAPA, nonconformance, root-cause analysis, risk management, process validation and control, measurement systems, and data-driven continuous improvement.
* Ability to identify and communicate material product, customer, and compliance risk and to influence operational and executive decisions with sound evidence and judgment.
* Experience building teams, developing leaders, and driving change across a matrixed or decentralized organization.
* Ability and willingness to travel regularly within the United States and Europe.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience in precision manufacturing serving medical device, aerospace, life sciences, or other regulated and quality-sensitive markets.
* Experience in an acquisition-driven, or rapidly scaling organization.
* Experience conducting quality due diligence and integrating acquired manufacturing businesses, sites, or quality systems.
* Experience with electronic quality management systems, quality data architecture, or digital quality transformation.
* Working knowledge of applicable medical device regulations and audit programs, such as FDA QMSR, EU MDR, or MDSAP.
* Lead Auditor, ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Quality Engineer, or Lean Six Sigma certification.
* Experience leading quality across the United States and Europe.

We're looking for talented individuals who share our passion for excellence and innovation.
  
  
**Position Overview**
This role provides senior leadership and ownership of the functions that safeguard product integrity and the operating environment: Quality, Compliance (Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Safety and regulatory conformance), Security, and Facilities. The position is accountable for ensuring that products consistently meet quality specifications, that operations remain fully compliant with regulatory and safety standards, that the site and its products are secure, and that facilities are maintained to support a reliable 24/7 manufacturing environment. The role establishes clear metrics and ownership across these areas and reports performance to senior leadership.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Quality: Establish and maintain quality control protocols for raw materials, components, and finished products. Design inspection and testing processes and provide guidance on maintaining consistent quality from the beginning of production through final release. Lead Quality Assurance and Quality Control teams, monitor quality metrics, and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to eliminate root causes of defects. Ensure conformance to customer, product, and industry specifications.
* Compliance: Ensure full compliance of operations with ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and applicable safety standards in accordance with New Jersey law. Own audits, certifications, and documentation, and serve as the primary liaison with regulatory bodies, auditors, and customers on compliance matters. Identify potential risks and pitfalls (e.g., equipment failures or other disruptions) and develop strategies to mitigate these issues through process improvement, alternative suppliers of materials, or altered equipment.
* Security: Oversee physical and product security programs consistent with the company's trust and authentication mission. Establish and enforce protocols to protect raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods, and sensitive assets throughout the facility and supply chain. Ensure operations meet payment-industry and customer security requirements, and manage security personnel and access controls across all shifts.
* Accountability: Own the key performance indicators and reporting for quality, compliance, security, and facilities. Establish clear ownership, metrics, and dashboards, report performance to senior management, and foster a culture of accountability across the organization. Manage a team of approximately 35 people across 7 shifts supporting QA, Safety & Security.
* Facilities: Oversee facility operations, maintenance, and environmental health and safety of the buildings, grounds, and utilities. Ensure facilities are maintained to support a reliable 24/7 manufacturing environment, manage facility vendors and contractors, and lead facility-related capital projects, space planning, and safe-workplace initiatives.

* Statistical process control (SPC) and data-driven decision making

* OSHA, EPA, ISO 14001 (environmental), ISO 45001 (occupational health & safety)

* Environmental compliance (emissions, waste management, hazmat handling)

**Spartronics, LLC**

**Career Opportunity: Site Director of Operations**

**Location:**
North Logan, Utah

**Employment Type:**
Full-Time | Salaried | Exempt

**Work Arrangement:**
On-Site

**Schedule:**
Full-Time, Monday–Friday

**Reports To:**
Vice President of Operations – West / Logan Site Leader

**Who We Are**

At
**Spartronics**
, we build more than electronics. We build the technology that powers critical applications across aerospace and defense, medical devices, life sciences, and industrial markets.

As a leading provider of electronic manufacturing services (EMS), Spartronics specializes in complex, high-reliability products, including printed circuit board assemblies (PCBA), electromechanical assemblies, integrated systems, and complete product manufacturing solutions.

**Career Opportunity: Director of Operations**

Spartronics is seeking an experienced
**Director of Operations**
to lead manufacturing operations and drive operational excellence at our North Logan, Utah facility.

This senior leadership position is responsible for the overall performance, execution, and continuous improvement of the site's operational functions, including Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Materials Planning, while providing indirect operational oversight and cross-functional partnership with Program Management.

Reporting to the Vice President of Operations – West / Logan Site Leader, the Director of Operations will establish operational priorities, develop high-performing teams, optimize manufacturing processes, and ensure the organization consistently achieves its safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability objectives.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader with strong business acumen, experience managing multiple operational disciplines, and a proven ability to drive results in complex, highly regulated manufacturing environments.

**What You Will Do**

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for the facility, translating organizational objectives into actionable plans, performance expectations, and measurable results.
* Direct Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Materials Planning functions, ensuring effective coordination, accountability, and alignment with site and corporate objectives.
* Provide indirect operational oversight and strategic partnership to Program Management, ensuring alignment between customer requirements, program execution, operational capacity and business objectives.
* Direct manufacturing operations, production planning, capacity management, and resource allocation, balancing changing customer demand, product complexity, and manufacturing constraints to achieve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity objectives.
* Establish operational priorities, evaluate performance against key metrics, and implement corrective actions to address performance gaps and emerging risks.
* Provide leadership and oversight of engineering activities, including process optimization, technical problem resolution, manufacturing readiness, new product introduction, and product transfers.
* Ensure the effectiveness of quality management systems, regulatory compliance, product conformity, and corrective and preventive action processes while preserving Quality's independent authority over product acceptance and compliance decisions.
* Oversee supply chain and materials planning activities, including procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, material availability, and production support.
* Partner with Program Management and other customer-facing functions to address delivery commitments, operational concerns, customer escalations, and changing business requirements.
* Develop operational budgets, resource plans, capital expenditure priorities, and cost improvement initiatives in collaboration with Finance, supporting achievement of site financial objectives and profitability targets..
* Evaluate operational and financial performance, identifying opportunities to improve profitability, reduce waste, control costs, and optimize resource utilization.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives utilizing Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, root cause analysis, and other structured problem-solving methodologies.
* Ensure manufacturing processes, product traceability, configuration and change control, and supporting documentation comply with applicable customer, industry, regulatory, and company requirements.
* Promote a strong safety culture and ensure operational compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety requirements.
* Establish and maintain structured operational performance management systems, including KPI reviews, cross-functional accountability, issue escalation, and corrective action follow-through to support timely, data-driven decision-making.
* Build, coach, and develop operational leadership teams, establishing clear performance expectations, succession plans, and workforce competency and development priorities.
* Collaborate with Human Resources on workforce planning, staffing requirements, employee performance, organizational development, and retention strategies.
* Coordinate with Facilities, Security, and other support functions to address infrastructure needs, operational continuity, physical security requirements, and business risks.
* Evaluate manufacturing capacity, technology, equipment, and infrastructure needs to support business growth, operational scalability, and capital investment decisions.
* Identify and mitigate operational risks associated with production disruptions, supplier constraints, quality concerns, regulatory requirements, and customer commitments.
* Represent site operations in corporate leadership discussions, customer interactions, audits, and strategic planning activities, communicating performance, priorities, and resource requirements.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support organizational objectives.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline; an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing operations, including at least five years in a senior leadership capacity overseeing multiple operational functions.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations with accountability for production, engineering, quality, supply chain, and cross-functional business objectives.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, production planning, capacity management, materials management, and operational performance improvement.
* Demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing engineering principles, process controls, technical problem resolution, and new product introduction activities.
* Working knowledge of quality management systems, regulatory compliance, product conformity, corrective action processes, and applicable manufacturing standards.
* Proven ability to develop and execute operational strategies, establish performance objectives, and achieve measurable improvements in quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience utilizing financial metrics, cost management practices, capital planning processes, and profitability analysis to drive operational decision-making.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and hold accountable cross-functional management teams while promoting collaboration and organizational effectiveness.
* Experience applying Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and structured problem-solving methodologies to complex operational challenges.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and decision-making skills, with the ability to evaluate competing priorities, manage operational risks, and resolve complex business issues.
* Advanced proficiency with business and manufacturing information systems, including ERP/MRP platforms, Microsoft Office applications, and data analysis and reporting tools. Demonstrated ability to interpret operational and financial data, evaluate performance trends, and leverage technology to support strategic planning and informed decision-making.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with employees, senior leadership, customers, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to manage sensitive business information, exercise sound judgment, and maintain confidentiality in accordance with company and applicable security requirements.
* Ability to read, write, speak, and comprehend English sufficiently to interpret technical documentation, communicate operational requirements, and perform essential job responsibilities.
* Ability to work full-time on-site at the assigned company facility in Logan, UT.

**Security Clearance Requirement**

Candidates must possess current, verifiable eligibility for a U.S. Government Secret-level security clearance or be willing and able to complete the necessary documentation to initiate the company-sponsored clearance process within 60 days of hire. The ability to obtain and maintain the required security clearance eligibility is a continuing condition of employment. Employment may continue while an appropriately initiated clearance application is pending, subject to company authorization and applicable security restrictions. A final determination of ineligibility, denial, or loss of required clearance eligibility will result in disqualification from the position and may result in termination of employment, subject to applicable law and company policy.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Leadership experience within electronics manufacturing services (EMS), printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), or high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environments.
* Experience with surface mount technology (SMT), through-hole assembly, electromechanical assembly, manufacturing test, and related electronics manufacturing processes.
* Experience supporting aerospace, defense, medical device, or other highly regulated manufacturing industries.
* Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, applicable IPC standards, and customer-specific quality requirements.
* Knowledge of ITAR, controlled technical information, and security requirements applicable to defense-related manufacturing.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or other recognized continuous improvement credentials.
* APICS/ASCM certification, such as CPIM or CSCP, or equivalent supply chain management credentials.
* Experience leading operational transformations, facility expansions, production transfers, or significant manufacturing improvement initiatives.
* Experience utilizing business intelligence platforms, advanced reporting tools, and integrated manufacturing systems to monitor operational performance and support continuous improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated success managing complex customer relationships, operational escalations, and cross-functional business challenges.

**Key Metrics and Focus Areas**

* Workplace safety performance and regulatory compliance.
* On-time delivery performance and production schedule attainment.
* Manufacturing efficiency, throughput, and capacity utilization.
* Product quality, first-pass yield, and cost of poor quality.
* Inventory accuracy, material availability, and inventory turns.
* Supplier delivery, quality, and overall performance.
* Operating cost performance, budget adherence, and profitability.
* Engineering responsiveness, manufacturing readiness, and successful new product introductions.
* Program execution support and fulfillment of customer commitments.
* Continuous improvement results, waste reduction, and operational efficiency.
* Quality management system effectiveness, audit performance, and corrective action closure.
* Workforce productivity, employee development, retention, and leadership effectiveness.
* Operational risk management, business continuity, and capacity readiness.

**Why This Role Matters**

As
**Director of Operations,**
you will play a critical role in shaping the performance, operational capabilities, and continued growth of our North Logan manufacturing facility. Your leadership will directly influence how effectively we deliver complex, high-reliability electronic products to customers operating in some of the world's most demanding industries. This is an opportunity to lead talented teams, strengthen operational performance, implement meaningful improvements, and contribute to the long-term success of a growing manufacturing organization.

**Benefits – Why Join Spartronics?**

At Spartronics, we recognize that our employees are essential to our success. We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, financial well-being, and professional development of our team members.

Benefits may include:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
* 401(k) retirement savings plan.
* Paid time off and company-paid holidays.
* Company-paid life insurance and disability benefits.
* Employee assistance and wellness resources.
* Professional development and career growth opportunities.
* Opportunities to contribute to innovative products supporting mission-critical industries.

*Specific benefits and eligibility are subject to applicable plan documents and company policies.*

**Physical Requirements and Work Location**

* Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments, including regular movement throughout production, warehouse, and operational areas.
* Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods, with occasional bending and reaching.
* Ability to occasionally lift, carry, or move materials weighing up to 25 pounds.
* Ability to operate computers and standard office equipment.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment when entering designated manufacturing areas.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Work Authorization & ITAR Requirements**

Due to the nature of certain products, technologies, and customer requirements, this position may involve access to export-controlled technical data or defense-related information subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and other applicable export control laws. Candidates must meet applicable U.S. export control authorization requirements and be eligible to access controlled technical information as required by the position. For this position, additional U.S. Government security clearance eligibility requirements apply, as described above.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

*Spartronics is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Veteran/Disabled 41 CFR 60-1.4. We comply with federal Affirmative Action guidelines in all employment opportunities for qualified employees and applicants.Employment at Spartronics is considered at-will, meaning that either the employee or Spartronics may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause, and with or without prior notification.*

**Description**
**THE COMPANY**
For over 40 years, Aero Simulation, Inc. (ASI) has provided quality flight training devices to the US Military. ASI has successfully built numerous training systems with a primary focus on aircrew and maintenance training systems. Our current programs include, but are not limited to, the B-1 Training Systems (Air Force), E-2D Training Systems (Navy), CH-53E Training Devices (USMC), IMOMS (Coast Guard), Navigation, Seamanship, Shiphandling Trainer – NSST (Navy). To learn more about ASI visit Programs- Aero Simulation, Inc.
  
  
ASI is a 100% employee-owned engineering and manufacturing company committed to supporting the nation’s warfighters. Being 100% employee-owned directly impacts our culture: it drives our decision-making, motivates our teams, increases our productivity, improves retention and contributes to the future success of our company. Our culture is one where we work hard for our clients and for each other – and we have fun collaborating, sharing experience and expertise, and learning along the way. We strive to deliver exceptional quality, elevate client relationships, and enrich the careers and lives of our employee-owners. As Employee-Owners, we are invested in the success and continued development of each other and the company.

ASI is a great place to build a career and grow with a company that is dedicated to quality, service and to fostering a community of support for each and every member of the team. To learn more about this opportunity, keep reading!
  
  
**Position Summary**

Based in Tampa, Florida, and reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Director of Production will oversee Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing through functional managers and department leads. *Workforce Leadership & Development*

* Lead, mentor, and develop production managers, supervisors, manufacturing engineers, technicians, assemblers, and integration personnel.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability standards for functional managers.
* Develop staffing and workforce plans to support current and anticipated production requirements.
* Identify workforce development needs and implement appropriate training and cross-training initiatives.
* Build organizational depth through succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.
* Foster a culture centered on safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

*Materials Management & Supply Chain Coordination*

* Ensure effective coordination between Production and Procurement to maintain material availability and support production schedules.
* Monitor material shortages, supplier performance, inventory levels, and long-lead procurement requirements.
* Establish appropriate material priorities based on program schedules and contractual commitments.
* Ensure effective inventory management, material traceability, and control of customer-furnished and government-furnished property.

* Promote a culture of quality and adherence to approved manufacturing processes throughout the production organization.

*Budget, Cost Control & Performance*

* Develop and manage production budgets, labor forecasts, and operational resource plans.
* Monitor production costs, labor utilization, productivity, rework, and overhead.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce waste, and increase production throughput.
* Evaluate production capacity and capital equipment requirements.
* Provide regular operational and financial performance reporting to the COO and executive leadership.
* Support long-term resource planning and investment strategies aligned with anticipated business growth.

*Facility Management & Workplace Safety*

* Provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
* Establish strategic priorities for facility readiness, infrastructure reliability, maintenance, and workplace safety.
* Ensure facilities, equipment, and infrastructure adequately support current production requirements and future growth.
* Review facility performance, safety metrics, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate facility investment, capital requirements, and infrastructure planning with the Facilities Manager and COO.
* Promote a safe, organized, and efficient working environment.

*Continuous Improvement*

* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, and other operational excellence methodologies, as appropriate.
* Establish consistent production management practices, standard operating procedures, and performance measures.
* Identify opportunities to reduce cycle times, eliminate waste, improve first-pass yield, and increase productivity.
* Drive corrective and preventive actions to resolve recurring operational issues.
* Promote employee engagement, proactive problem-solving, and continuous

**LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS**

* Provides leadership and direct supervision of Group Leaders responsible for Manufacturing, Facility Management, Production Control, Workplace Safety, and Stockroom operations, establishing priorities, expectations, and accountability for operational performance, quality, efficiency, safety, and on-time delivery.
* The Director maintains oversight of these functional areas while ensuring alignment with program requirements and organizational objectives. Ensures teams have the resources, processes, equipment, capabilities, and organizational support necessary to maintain safe and efficient operations, support successful program execution, and meet production schedules and contractual commitments.

You will also oversee material management to maximize the efficiency of high-volume grades. Partner closely with Maintenance and Tooling teams to minimize changeover downtime, and enforce rigorous preventive maintenance programs.

**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.
  
  

* Perform all documentation in compliance with ALCOA++ principles and site SOPs.
* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

****Panther: Better Health Is Skin Deep****
Panther is building the leading skin-powered treatment delivery and data platform for health and longevity. Its proprietary intradermal SmartPatch™ precisely delivers treatments to activate local and systemic healing, unlocking the skin as a scalable gateway for care. Panther’s AI-based platform accelerates partners’ product development and personalizes treatment, resulting in compelling consumer and provider experiences. Panther is targeting economically attractive markets of increasing clinical and regulatory difficulty, starting with its PIQUE™ branded Skincare products in mid-2027, and rapidly progressing to Medical Aesthetics and Therapeutics thereafter. Panther’s platform, significant IP portfolio and staged regulatory strategy provide a defensible moat. Panther is led by a team of successful entrepreneurs and operators and is advised by leading scientific experts.
  
  
**The Opportunity**
Panther Life Sciences is building a new category of consumer-centric health and beauty products powered by our SmartPatch platform. As we move from development into commercialization, manufacturing becomes the critical unlock for scale, quality, and customer trust.
  
  
We are seeking a Director of Manufacturing Operations to own this transition end-to-end. This role is responsible for translating innovative R&D into reliable, high-quality, and scalable commercial production across both cosmetic and medical device products. You will lead the build-out of Panther's manufacturing strategy, serving as the bridge between internal development teams and external CMO partners.
  
  
You will define how manufacturing operates at Panther, from selecting and standing up partners, to leading technology transfer, to building the systems that allow us to scale from thousands to millions of units. This is not a maintenance role. You will be building the manufacturing function from scratch. Your work will directly impact product availability, customer experience, and the company's ability to grow.
  
  
You will work closely with the leadership team and cross-functional team members in formulation, device development, and quality to establish a manufacturing engine that supports both near-term commercial goals and long-term platform expansion. This is for someone who wants to build, scale, and set the standard for manufacturing in a category-defining company with a great team and a platform that is already generating clinical results. If you want to build something that matters, we want to hear from you.
  
  
Some travel will required approximately 10% -30%
  
  
This role is ideally based in Pittsburgh, with New York as an alternative location."
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**CDMO & Manufacturing Operations**

* Serve as the primary relationship owner and day-to-day point of contact for CMO partners
* Lead technology transfer from R&D to clinical and commercial manufacturing
* Oversee late-stage clinical and commercial production across product lines
* Drive manufacturing performance metrics including yield, throughput, and product quality
* Support CMO selection and onboarding, including process validation and scale-up
* Build and manage supply chain, logistics, fulfillment, and inventory operations
* Own material sourcing and supplier relationships
* Identify critical dependencies and build supplier redundancy to mitigate risk

**Scaling, Systems & Financial Planning**

* Build the manufacturing line from the ground up with a path from ~10K to ~1M units per month
* Drive automation, process optimization, and line redesign as production scales
* Own manufacturing cost modeling and financial planning (FP&A) for operations
* Develop sourcing strategy and budget frameworks in partnership with finance and leadership
* Establish systems and processes to support future team growth and internal manufacturing capabilities

**Quality, Compliance & Cross-Functional Leadership**

* Ensure manufacturing quality, regulatory compliance, and adherence to QMS
* Partner cross-functionally with leadership, formulation, device, and quality teams
* Contribute to customer satisfaction through reliable product delivery and issue resolution

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience scaling a product from R&D to commercial manufacturing in a regulated environment
* Experience overseeing manufacturing operations for a Class II or III medical device or equivalent regulated product
* Hands-on experience scaling production volumes significantly (e.g., 10x or more)
* Direct experience working with CMO partners including selection, onboarding, and tech transfer
* Experience managing supply chain, logistics, inventory, and fulfillment operations
* Familiarity with Quality Management Systems (QMS) in regulated environments
* Demonstrated ability to lead technology transfer and process scale-up
* Experience with manufacturing cost modeling and financial planning
* Direct people management experience

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with combination products (drug + device), such as auto-injectors, EpiPens, nasal sprays, or microarray-based systems
* Background in Material Science & Technology Transfer (MSNT)
* Experience scaling production to high-volume output (100K+ units per month)
* Experience across both cosmetic and medical device products
* Experience with automation and line redesign in a manufacturing scale-up context
* Background in customer support or customer-facing operations within manufacturing
* Experience managing managers or building multi-layered organizations
* Strong systems orientation with experience implementing or optimizing operational infrastructure

**Benefits**

* Build something unique and high-impact with a world-class team of experts in technology, healthcare, and science.
* Equity in the form of stock options
* Competitive health insurance, including 90% employer-paid medical, plus dental and vision
* Life, AD&D and short-term disability insurance
* Paid time off and paid company holidays
* In-person company events
* Fully stocked kitchen

Panther Life Sciences is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital or partnership status, age, national origin, citizenship, veteran or military status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, caregiver status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

*Richelieu Foods, Inc. is a leading national private label and contract packing food manufacturer focused on frozen pizza. We have two manufacturing facilities located in IL and WI. We provide products to many national retailers, wholesalers, distributors, club and mass stores, as well as industrial accounts including other food manufacturers.*
**Job Summary**
At Richelieu Foods we are making Great Food from Great People. We are looking for an experienced Director of Plant Operations who is comfortable driving transformation while reinforcing a culture of support and development. The Director of Plant Operations will report directly to the Senior Director of Operations with significant exposure to the Richelieu Senior Leadership Team. The Director of Plant Operations will lead the manufacturing operations for the facility, producing quality products in a people and food-safe manner, at or below budgeted cost. The position will be responsible for ensuring plant operations follow all regulatory, quality and safety standards. This role will be responsible for driving continuous improvement initiatives, striving to deliver zero loss and 100% employee engagement in support of Richelieu’s integrated manufacturing strategy.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Create a high-performance operations team by recruiting and developing teams with an appropriate mix of experience, capabilities, and skills to consistently meet company goals and departmental initiatives in the most cost-effective manner. Ensure effective succession planning for all pivotal positions.
* Create and efficiently manage four key divisions of operations: 1) Manufacturing 2) Maintenance 3) Materials and 4) Operational excellence. Understand the financial impacts of various sourcing, labor, materials and overhead strategies on the business and act accordingly to maximize returns.
* Support new projects for the business, engaging suppliers to help the team understand any costs and design implication. Ability to engage and collaborate cross-functionally to facilitate commercialization of new products and partnering closely with the leadership team to support the broader activities and initiatives.
* Manage KPI's to include (but not limited to): Safety, Quality, People, Service, and Cost
* Manage technology and process improvement projects to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the operations function.
* Plan, organize and direct the manufacturing operations ensuring the plant meets the daily production schedule, producing products that meet or exceed established standards.
* Establish and communicate clear metric targets and results. Develop and execute plans that drive improved operational performance.
* Participate in the development, implementation & evaluation of business goals that deliver strategic business objectives.
* Develop and execute job training programs that build the capability of the factory and leadership team members, including skill-based pay for the factory team and succession planning for the leadership team.
* Teach and deploy lean six-sigma tools such as daily direction setting, 5S, equipment center lining, defect handling and root cause failure analysis that drive towards zero loss and 100% employee engagement.
* Manage budget and cost controls considering changes in demand (volume), business seasonality and required service levels.
* Identify manufacturing cost drivers and proactively adjust manpower and department expenses to achieve budget commitments.
* Daily focus on yields with a particular focus on raw and pack materials. Actively participate in the KPI calls to report on results and improvement plans.
* Ensure the plant meets OSHA requirements and continually improve safety record by addressing both physical safety issues as well as employee safety attitudes. Cultivate a safety culture. Ensure compliance with all food regulatory requirements and adherence to food safety and GMP's.
* Maintain superior scores on all SQF or other third-party audits (customer driven).
* Ensure all products meet product specifications and consumer / customer complaints are fully investigated and addressed.
* Participate in the development of the strategic plan for the factory including the development of the annual operating budget and quarterly forecasts.
* Inspire the team and be the voice of the company’s core values, to motivate and capture personal commitment in creating a pathway to both their individual and our collective long-term success and growth.

**POSITION PURPOSE**

This position is responsible for leading, planning, organizing, and managing the safe and efficient operation and maintenance of the Bison Generation Station (BGS) facility to economically produce electricity to satisfy member needs.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES**

* Provide technical input for the decision-making process in power plant operation and maintenance. Keep plant staff informed of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of the facility and implement necessary corrective actions.
* Manage plant operational equipment; develop and maintain plant personnel and equipment safety standards; and develop preventative maintenance procedures and operational procedure manuals.
* Support the safety program by rigorously assuring standards are enforced and safety is at the forefront of all actions.
* Work in collaboration with other departments to build and adhere to all project budgets; responsible for developing and adhering to the BGS Long-Range Engineering Plan and the Capital Budget.
* Supervise the selection, training, development, and supervision of BGS employees.
* Evaluate the performance of plant section heads reporting to the position, review performance evaluations for all employees, and recommend salary adjustments for plant employees.
* Direct the development and submission of required reports to assure documentation and communication of plant operations, maintenance, and environmental activities.
* Authorize all plant purchase request orders and staff timesheets. In addition, review all proposed changes or modifications to plant systems or equipment and proposed tests or research programs.
* Responsible for staff development to ensure that each section functions safely and efficiently and that they all work together to meet the goals and objectives of Basin Electric, the plant operations division, and the station.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in Energy Management, Business, or an Engineering Accreditation Commission/ Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (EAC/ABET) accredited engineering program; and 10 years of related power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance, or engineering experience; or
* An associate’s degree in Power/Process Plan Technology or related field; and 12 years’ experience in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering; or
* A high school diploma or equivalent (GED or HSED); and 14 years’ in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering.
* Prior supervisory experience.
* A valid driver’s license.

**PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS**

This position requires constant sitting; and occasional lifting/carrying up to 50 pounds, pushing/pulling up to 20 pounds, standing, walking, bending, crawling, reaching, and climbing. This position uses office equipment and field tools. This position also requires finger dexterity, good vision/hearing, hand coordination, and the ability to perform close work, analyze data/reports, conduct research, and implement recommendations. This position occasionally works in areas of dirt/dust, fumes, chemicals, extreme heat/cold, vibration, noise, and poor ventilation. This position must be respirator qualified.

**KEY SKILLS**

* Effective administrative and human relation skills.
* Excellent organizational, written and verbal communication skills.
* Proficient with personal computers and Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
* Able to provide work direction, develop plans/procedures/goals, and present information to others.

**A ROLE THAT SUPPORTS YOUR CAREER AND YOUR FUTURE**

* Competitive salary aligned with experience.
* Relocation package to support your transition.
* Up to 15% 401(k) match.
* More benefits to support you.

**To learn more about Bison Generation Station, please use the following link: https://www.basinelectric.com/about-us/Generation/Bison-Generation-Station**

Applicants interested in this opening should go to careers.basinelectric.com to apply. Employees must apply through Careers in SAP SuccessFactors.

* Equipment: Verify that all plant equipment is in good working condition and all preventative maintenance is being performed on a scheduled basis. Review and approve all work orders. Review all daily maintenance activity reports. Develop capital justifications to update equipment as needed.
* Environmental: Review of Air Quality annual reports. Review and coordinate completion of Annual Form R for EPA/Health Department. Review and coordinate completion of Annual Hazardous Materials Inventory and Business Plan. Perform other duties, as necessary.
* Safety: Review Safety program and training with EHS management. Daily observation during plant audit will include safety. Check each department and observe employee safety procedures. Member of the Food Safety Team and Food Quality Team.

* Coordinate on the job training.
* Oversee adherence to company policies and procedures.
* Oversee scheduling of management, employees, and temporary labor.
* Have the responsibility of reviewing timesheets, overtime and approve payroll.

* Must have the ability to trouble shoot problems and be persistent until a solution is found.
* Must work in a safe manner and follow all safety procedures including use of safety equipment.
* Must be willing to ask for assistance when the process is unclear.
* Proficient in verbal and written communication skills. Must be able to communicate with upper management on a daily basis.
* Leadership, team development, coaching, and / or teaching experience.
* Good math and statistical skills.
* Excellent computer skills for data input, report writing, program tracking.
* Excellent organizational and follow through skills.

**Education And/Or Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Dairy or Food Science and four years of experience in a Plant leadership role in a Dairy or Food Manufacturing facility is strongly desired.

We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!
  
  
In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by
*TIME*
as a “Best Invention”,
*MIT Technology Review*
as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and
*Fast Company*
as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.
  
  
Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.
  
  
**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**
Role Description
  
  
As the Senior Manager of Assembly Manufacturing Engineering, you will serve as the primary architect of the production lifecycle, bridging the gap between research prototypes and high-volume factory operations. You will lead a multidisciplinary team of engineers to develop and internalize robust manufacturing processes for both battery enclosures and module/pack assembly—including robotic joining, sealing, electrolyte filling, and leak testing. By owning the full equipment lifecycle, from defining detailed user requirements through to factory testing and final site commissioning, you ensure that production lines are world-class, delivering a "machine that builds the machine" with precision and technical rigor.
  
  
Strategically, your objective is to drive operational scale by ensuring products are designed specifically for ease of manufacturing and assembly during the earliest development phases. You will champion a data-driven culture that utilizes failure mode analysis and advanced root-cause investigation to reduce production risks and achieve aggressive targets for quality, output rate, and equipment uptime. By fostering collaboration between Product Design, Quality, and Supply Chain, you will manage the critical transition from initial design to full-scale production, ensuring that every process is statistically validated to guarantee long-term reliability and cost-effectiveness.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Lead the development and optimization of battery manufacturing processes for battery assembly manufacturing.
* Ensure highly capable processes are identified and demonstrated for our production facilities ahead of detailed equipment design.
* Oversee the design and implementation of manufacturing processes such as: manual and robotic assembly, joining, sealing, system leak testing, and quality checks to achieve optimal performance and reliability.
* Collaborate with product design team, R&D, quality, and supply chain, to translate product requirements into a battery design and manufacturing process that achieve our company targets.
* Collaborate cross functionally to develop and maintain PFMEA, process specifications, measurement systems GR&R, control plan, and quality inspection methods (incoming, outgoing, and in-process).
* Lead troubleshooting efforts to identify root causes of manufacturing issues and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
* Internalize responsibility for delivery of equipment and processes that enable the operations team to achieve factory production metrics (quality, yield, rate, and availability).
* Identify trends/correlations, and make data-driven decisions for process optimization.

**What You'll Bring**

* Hands-on experience in a high-volume manufacturing organization.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering.
* 10 years of experience in engineering roles within battery manufacturing or a related industry, with expertise in complex assembly processes. 4+ leading technical teams.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing equipment procurement, setup, and commissioning, including a clear understanding of equipment qualification and validation protocols.
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing principles and their application in a high-volume production environment.
* Proven track record of successfully leading cross-functional teams in the development and optimization of manufacturing processes for electrochemical systems.
* Proficiency in process engineering principles, statistical analysis, and quality management systems for process optimization and improvement.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and convey technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.
* Leadership and mentoring abilities with a commitment to fostering a culture of continuous learning and accelerated innovation through quick iteration.
* Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment is a plus.

*This opportunity is based out of Form Factory 1 – Form Energy’s 550,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility located in Weirton, WV, a commutable distance from Pittsburgh. Purpose-built for high-volume, advanced battery production, Form Factory 1 is a hub of fast-moving, collaborative work driving a new era of large-scale American energy manufacturing in the heart of the Rust Belt.*
*Relocation assistance is available.*
*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*
*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*
