existing_roles.description:
**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS**

*Ritchey Livestock ID* | Fort Collins, Colorado | Full-Time, Onsite

Run the Operation. Build the Team. Shape What's Next.

**This Role Is For Builders.**

**We're looking for someone who can run a great operation today—and help build the company we'll become tomorrow.**

At Ritchey Livestock ID, we believe farmers and ranchers are the unsung heroes of our world. They work long hours, in every kind of weather, doing the essential work of feeding the rest of us. They don't ask for much in return. The least we can do is get our little part right.

For more than 60 years, we've manufactured livestock identification tags that ranchers can count on. Our products may be small, but the responsibility we feel to our customers is anything but.

We're a profitable, growing American manufacturer with a loyal nationwide customer base. We've recently completed the largest facility investment in our company's history, opening a new manufacturing operation in Fort Collins, Colorado. Now we're building the people, systems, and culture to carry Ritchey into its next chapter.

**We're looking for a hands-on Director of Operations who can lead that effort—and potentially grow into a broader executive leadership role as the company evolves.**

This is not a position for someone who wants to lead from behind a desk. You'll spend meaningful time on the production floor, working alongside your managers, solving real problems, and helping people succeed.

You'll also be expected to think beyond today's production schedule: developing leaders, building systems, improving performance, and preparing Ritchey for its next stage of growth.

**The Opportunity**

You'll lead approximately 45 people across manufacturing, engraving, shipping, and related operations, working directly with our CEO.

Your mission is twofold: **Run an exceptional operation today. Build the people, processes, and accountability that make excellence repeatable tomorrow.**

You'll own performance across safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost, and team development.

You'll be responsible for developing department managers, improving operational systems, driving continuous improvement, and building a culture where people take pride in their work and ownership of their results.

**Your First Year: Real Challenges, Real Opportunity**

We've made a major investment in our future. Now comes the work of making that investment pay off.

Here are five challenges you'll help us tackle:

* **Strengthen our new manufacturing operation.** Continue ramping up our Fort Collins facility, improving production stability, quality, capacity, and efficiency.
* **Improve scheduling and throughput.** Build better production planning and workflows across manufacturing, engraving, and shipping to improve delivery performance and reduce bottlenecks.
* **Build systems that last.** Reduce dependence on individual employees by developing practical SOPs, standardized processes, clear performance measures, and repeatable operating routines.
* **Develop our next generation of leaders.** Coach newer managers, strengthen accountability, and build employee development practices that help great people grow.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Use Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and practical root-cause problem-solving to reduce waste, improve productivity, and create measurable, sustainable improvements.

You'll have meaningful ownership of these challenges, the support of our leadership team, and the freedom to make a lasting impact.

**Who We're Looking For**

We're looking for a rare combination of heart, head, and hands. Someone who can lead people, build systems, solve problems, and roll up their sleeves when the work demands it.

**What you must bring:**

* **Proven People Leadership:** Demonstrated success leading teams in a manufacturing or production environment, ideally 20 or more employees, with experience developing supervisors or managers and holding people accountable.
* **Demonstrated Systems Building:** A track record of improving processes, implementing operational improvements, and building systems that continue to work without your constant involvement.
* **High Agency & Ownership:** The judgment, initiative, work ethic, and follow-through to take responsibility for results, solve difficult problems, and lead confidently in a hands-on environment.

**What we'd love to see:**

* Experience in plastic injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methods. Certifications are valued but not required.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, purchasing, and quality systems.
* Strong financial and analytical skills, with an understanding of how operational decisions affect profitability.
* Experience developing managers, building teams, and helping an organization prepare for growth.

We value experience, but we're far more interested in what you've accomplished than the number of years on your résumé.

**Seasoned plastics professionals and exceptional leaders from other manufacturing environments are equally encouraged to apply.** What matters most is demonstrated leadership, systems thinking, operational judgment, and a willingness to keep learning.

***The Ritchey Way***

Our culture is built around one simple commitment: **DO RIGHT BY THE RANCH.**

Four core principles guide how we show up every day:

**ASK WHY. ASK WHAT IF.** — Learn the work. Make it better.

**MAKE THE SMALL THINGS COUNT.** — Bring care to the details, seen or unseen.

**NO SIDELINES.** — See it. Say it. Help solve it.

**BE GOOD TO WORK WITH.** — Carry your share. Be good company.

These aren't just words on a wall. They're the standards we hold ourselves and each other to. As our Director of Operations, you'll help bring *The Ritchey Way* to life through your leadership, your example, and the team you build.

**Why Ritchey?**

We're small enough that your ideas matter, but established and ambitious enough that your work can make a lasting difference. You'll have direct access to ownership, real authority to drive improvement, and a genuine opportunity to help shape the company's future.

**We're intentionally looking for someone with the potential to grow beyond operations.**

For the right individual who demonstrates exceptional leadership, business judgment, and results, this role could become a pathway toward broader company leadership, potentially including a future President or General Manager position.

That opportunity isn't guaranteed or tied to a timetable. It will be earned through performance, trust, and demonstrated ability to lead an increasingly complex business.

Most importantly, you'll be part of a team that takes pride in showing up every day for the farmers and ranchers who feed us.

**If you're a builder at heart, believe great people deserve great leadership, and want to create something you can be genuinely proud of, we'd love to meet you.**

**Location:** Fort Collins, Colorado — Full-Time, Onsite

**Compensation:** $130,000–$160,000 base salary, depending on experience and qualifications, plus performance-based bonus..

Pay: $130,000.00 - $160,000.00 per year

* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance

* How many years of practical experience do you have with concepts such as six sigma and lean manufacturing?

**DEFINITION:**

Under general direction from the General Manager, plans, directs, organizes, integrates and provides oversight of ReGen Monterey’s Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), equipment maintenance, site and facilities maintenance, landfill operations; scales operations, landfill gas operations, and Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) operations; directs and manages the development of short and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the Strategic Plan and annual business plan and ensures their effective execution; ensures all assigned operations and functions serve the needs of ReGen Monterey, while complying with applicable laws and regulations; responsible for maximizing the environmental management of resources; provides highly responsible and complex operations support to the General Manager.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

This position is responsible for coordination, integration and short and long-range planning of a wide variety of functions related to solid waste processing, recycling and diversion programs for ReGen Monterey. Incumbents work at an advanced professional level on complex and specialized solid waste-related operations, recycling activities, facilities, programs, and services, which include formulation and implementation of programs and financial budgets. Within assigned areas of accountability, the incumbent operates with substantial latitude and discretion to achieve effective and efficient utilization of resources in serving ReGen Monterey’s mission. Positions at this class level serve as a member of ReGen’s leadership team and provide advice and counsel to the General Manager regarding strategic policy and problem-solving issues relating to the assigned Departments and ReGen’s overall. A person appointed to the Director of Operations classification is an “at-will” employee.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*The following duties are typical of this classification and are intended only to describe the various types of work that may be performed, the level of technical complexity of the assignment(s) and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties. The omission of a specific duty statement does not exclude it from the position if the work is consistent with the concept of the classification or is similar or closely related to another duty statement to address business needs and changing business practices.*

* Oversee and is responsible for planning and execution of all aspects of solid waste and recycling operations including processing, recycling/diversion, scheduling, expansion and renovation of processing facility, and customer service.
* Oversee logistics, material preparation and export compliance of collected materials and manage all aspects of commodity sales and related contracted services.
* Oversees and is responsible for the planning and execution of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of ReGen Monterey’s landfill; oversees proper compliance with specifications on the use and development of disposal site, ensures proper operations compliance with health and safety regulations.
* Participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities of ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Plans, organizes, controls, integrates and evaluates the work of assigned departments to ensure services comply with the policies and strategic direction set by the General Manager, Board of Directors and all applicable laws and regulations.
* Recommend and enforce State waste reduction/recycling regulations and other policy issues, including safety policy and procedures.
* Manages the development, revision, and implementation of policies and procedures for ReGen Monterey’s solid waste and recycling/diversion operations.
* Drafts budget for assigned departments.
* Reviews and assesses all program production data; measures program effectiveness; prepares quarterly and annual data reports.
* Assists in the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for equipment and services; represents the division in negotiations with vendors and service contractors and participates in contract administration in disputed contractual matters.
* Prepares staff reports and letters, including reports for presentation to Board of Directors.
* All ReGen Monterey positions require the employee to provide good customer service to both internal and external customers, maintain positive and effective working relationships with other ReGen Monterey employees, and have regular and reliable attendance and timeliness. Must show cooperation and respect to fellow employees and supervisors at all times.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:**

The incumbent in this position provides direct supervision of the operations department managers and has oversight of multiple departments and indirect supervision of approximately 100 assigned department employees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Through subordinates, supervises the safe and efficient handling and disposal of solid waste, including household, industrial, infectious, medical, and household hazardous materials; provides oversight ancillary solid waste operations, including equipment maintenance and repair, recycling, and enforcement of refuse disposal laws.
* Coordinates solid waste processing operations with engineering staff to ensure the success of new programs and facilities; analyzes field operations and formulates improvements to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations; performs long-range planning for staffing needs, equipment replacement, and other operational requirements.
* Provides oversight to HHW program and organics recycling program, including food waste collection, yard waste processing, mulch/compost marketing and other waste reduction processing such as scrap metal, electronic waste, mattresses, and scrap tires.

* Prepares tonnage reports and makes recommendations regarding change in fees.
* Organize and optimize the structure of the assigned departments, adjusting in accordance with workloads and new/changing functions.
* Maintain contact with various governmental and regulatory agencies, industry related agencies, and represent ReGen Monterey at public and professional organizations functions.
* Selects and trains operations staff; assists management staff in resolving the most difficult operational problems; establishes productive standards and measures staff performance; accordingly, prepares annual performance plans, evaluates performance, and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinate managers. Collaborates with human resources with disciplinary actions.
* Directly or through subordinates, responds to complaints from ReGen Monterey customers by explaining and enforcing applicable laws and regulations; participates in public workshops to explain and generate support for proposed projects and facilities; may address the Board of Directors to answer questions about issues or proposals related to ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Oversees and participates in the annual review and revision of ReGen Monterey’s fee structure; develops strategies and approaches for evaluating fee change alternatives; directs the development and recommends proposed fees; attends and participates in public meetings; oversees the implementation of new fees following board approval.
* Directs and coordinates the preparation of analyses and recommendations regarding policy issues and long-range plans to address ReGen Monterey’s financial needs; advises the General Manager regarding policy issues, programs and projects to meet ReGen Monterey and customer needs; advises and assists the General Manager in identifying, articulating and implementing policies, programs and projects.
* Participates in the analysis of proposed legislation and regulation; participates in industry and intergovernmental activities to influence legislative and regulatory change consistent with ReGen Monterey’s interests and needs; represents ReGen Monterey as requested or assigned in dealings with stakeholders in ReGen Monterey’s service area, and with other industry and governmental agencies and professional organizations.
* Participates in major negotiations with contractors, consultants, vendors, collective bargaining and other public agencies.
* Participates in regional, state, national and other professional meetings and conferences to stay abreast of trends and technology related to ReGen Monterey’s operations, particularly in areas of assigned accountability.

**Knowledge of and Ability to:**

The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to successfully perform the assigned duties.

**Knowledge of:**

Principles and practices of recycling and diversion program operations, solid waste management and landfill maintenance practices and procedures; local, state and federal regulations pertaining to environmental management of landfills and public works systems or landfill operations; California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); principles and practices of budgeting, effective management, supervision, evaluation and training; health and safety regulations. Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint) is required.

**Ability to:**

Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals; understand highly regulatory issues (current and proposed) and appropriate permitting for solid waste facilities, recycling operations and programs; negotiate with the best interest of ReGen Monterey; work independently with minimal supervision; manage and evaluate the work of others; prepare clear and concise plans, specifications, and technical reports; interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local policies, laws, and regulations; present proposals and recommendations clearly, logically and persuasively in public meetings; develop and implement appropriate procedures and controls; exercise sound, independent judgment within policy guidelines; develop and administer departmental goals, objectives, and procedures; analyze and assess programs, policies, and operational needs and make appropriate adjustments; research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods and techniques; facilitate group participation and consensus building; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

**TRAINING, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental planning and management; environmental studies; solid waste planning or a related field is required.

**Experience:**

* Ten to 15 years of broad and progressively responsible work experience in recycling program operations, transfer station management, or combined and related experiences.
* A minimum of five years of recent experience in solid waste management and/or in the operation of mixed waste processing facility or a single-stream material recovery facility or operation of a landfill is required. **OR** work experience in a management position with a private or public agency responsible for solid waste management, recycling/diversion or landfill operations to demonstrate knowledge, skills, and abilities to meet the above minimum requirements.

**License or Certificate:**

* Possession of or ability to obtain a certificate of Manager of Landfill Operations (MOLO) issued by the Solid Waste Association of North America (SWANA) is desired.
* Possession of a valid California driver’s license is required.

**PhYSICAL AND SENSORY REQUIREMENTS:**

The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by employees to successfully perform the essential functions of this class. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Physical Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to sit; talk or hear, in person, in meetings and by telephone; use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; and reach with hands and arms; occasionally bend, stoop, lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 25 pounds individually. Employees are occasionally required to walk and stand on even and uneven surfaces, grounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

**Mental Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to use written and oral communication skills; read and interpret complex data, information and documents; analyze and solve complex policy and operational problems; observe and interpret people and situations; use math and mathematical reasoning; learn and apply new information or skills; perform highly detailed work on multiple, concurrent tasks with constant interruptions; work under intensive deadlines and interact with Board members, all levels of ReGen Monterey management, other elected and appointed governmental officials, consultants, contractors, developers, vendors, employees, media representatives and the public.

**Special Demands**

Must be able to actively participate in public meetings, including giving presentations in person and on camera before the Board of Directors and members of the public.

**Work Environment**

Employees work under typical office conditions, and the noise level is usually quiet, occasional exposure to dirt, grease, foul odors and other outdoor elements.

existing_roles.title: Director, Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement
existing_roles.description:
**Lead the Operation. Elevate the System. Grow the People.**
============================================================

Imagine starting your day on the production floor—checking safety, huddling with supervisors, scanning your ERP dashboard, and walking a focused gemba to spot the next opportunity. By afternoon, you're aligning capacity plans to customer demand, unblocking material flow, and celebrating wins from a cross-functional Kaizen. This is the rhythm of our Director, Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement.

**Your Impact**
---------------

* Build, coach, and mentor a high-performing team of supervisors, leads, and skilled production personnel.
* Champion a culture that prizes safety, quality, accountability, and teamwork.
* Advance engagement through cross-training, development pathways, and clear performance expectations.
* Own production planning, scheduling, and capacity management to meet cost, quality, and delivery goals.
* Ensure on-time manufacturing and shipment while upholding rigorous quality standards.
* Lead Lean, Six Sigma, and CI roadmaps to lift throughput, reduce waste, and standardize best practices.
* Optimize processes to increase productivity and lower cost-to-serve.
* Manage material flow, inventory health, and operational KPIs end-to-end.
* Use ERP and data analytics to drive decisions and uncover improvement opportunities.
* Collaborate with senior leadership on long-range manufacturing strategies and investments.
* Recruit, develop, and retain exceptional manufacturing talent.

**Qualifications**
------------------

### **Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related technical field; or commensurate experience.
* 10+ years leading manufacturing operations with oversight of multiple production teams.
* Demonstrated success running large-scale operations and developing top-performing teams.
* Deep experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Quality Systems, and continuous improvement.
* Hands-on expertise with ERP, production planning, scheduling, and inventory management.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and sound decision-making skills.
* Excellent communicator and people leader.
* Proven ability to drive accountability while fostering a collaborative, positive workplace.

### **Preferred**

* Background in machining, welding, finishing, powder coating, assembly, or similar processes.
* Ability to read and interpret manufacturing drawings and specifications.
* History of improving productivity, quality, on-time delivery, and employee engagement.

**Who Thrives Here**
--------------------

A visible, floor-engaged leader who blends strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You enjoy solving problems shoulder-to-shoulder with your team and creating an environment where people perform, grow, and stay.

**About Amatrol**
-----------------

We equip learners and employers with hands-on training systems, interactive eLearning, simulators, curriculum, and certification resources that turn complex technology into practical skill. Our U.S.-made solutions serve schools, colleges, training centers, and industry across manufacturing, automation, robotics, electrical systems, oil and gas, packaging, and more—bridging learning and doing for today’s technical careers.

**Your Toolkit**
----------------

* Leadership / People Management
* Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
* Quality Control Experience
* Six Sigma Experience
* Production Planning & Scheduling
* Excellent Communication Skills
* Root Cause Analysis
* Process Development
* Blueprint Reading
* Microsoft Excel
* ERP Systems
* Hands On Leadership Style
* ISO 9001
* Manufacturing Leadership
* metal fabrication
* Microsoft Outlook
* Multiple Department Leadership
* Problem Solving
* Reporting
* Understanding Manufacturing Processes
* electronic assembly leadership

### **Tools You’ll Use**

* ERP Software

**Ready to Lead?**
------------------

If you’re eager to scale performance and build a best-in-class operation, we’d love to talk.

Please Note: This is a fully in-person position in Jeffersonville, IN. To be considered for this position, candidates must submit a current, chronological resume showing relevant work experience as well as a relevant digital portfolio. Contact Human Resources if you need any accommodations during the job application process due to a disability. Amatrol, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

This position is not eligible for placement by outside recruitment or staffing agencies.

Oak View Group:

Oak View Group (OVG) is the global leader in premium live entertainment infrastructure and services, with a platform spanning venue development and end-to-end capabilities across venue management, hospitality, and sponsorship sales. Founded in 2015, the company serves a collection of seven world-class owned venues and a client roster of the most iconic arenas, stadiums, convention centers, music festivals, performing arts centers, and cultural institutions, spanning four continents.

Position Summary:

In consultation with the General Manager, the **Director of Operations** directs the day-to-day operations of the complex, including but not limited to maintenance, setup/changeovers, custodial/housekeeping, equipment safety, and capital projects. This employee also provides overall administrative planning, direction, and policies to operating managers and supervisors, assuring the highest quality service program to ensure booking and rebooking of events. The Director of Operations ensures an effective and cost-efficient program by controlling the departmental operating budget while providing highly responsible staff assistance to the General Manager.

This role pays an annual salary of $80,000 - $88,000.

**Benefits for Full-Time Roles: Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance, 401(k) Savings Plan, 401(k) matching, and Paid Time Off (vacation days, sick days, and 11 holidays).**

**This position will remain open until February 19, 2027.**

Responsibilities:

* Direct overall daily operation and maintenance of the facility and all systems. This includes electrical, plumbing, fire protection, life safety, workplace safety, communications, scoreboard systems, pest control, custodial services, etc
* Participate in the development and administration of the facility’s operations and capital budgets; forecast additional funds needed for staffing, equipment, materials, and supplies; monitor and approve expenditures; implement adjustments as necessary
* Oversees the advancing and communicating of event information to the appropriate departments and staff
* Oversees the operation of event setup and teardown, i.e., basketball floor, stage risers, chairs, signs, banquet functions, etc
* Acts as liaison with City and County Services for numerous facility-related functions (city codes, parking, licenses, permits, inspections, warranties, etc.)
* Select, train, direct, motivate, and evaluate staff; provide or coordinate staff training; work with employees to correct deficiencies; implement discipline and termination procedures
* Responsible for health & safety compliance
* Develop and update comprehensive management reports and manuals (i.e., Operations Manual, Annual Preventative Maintenance Plan, Annual Facility Report, Fire Code Rules & Regulations, etc.)
* Demonstrate continuous effort to improve operations, decrease turnaround times, streamline work processes, and work cooperatively and jointly to provide quality seamless customer service
* Conduct a variety of organizational and operational studies; recommend modifications to programs, policies, and procedures as appropriate
* Establish and maintain effective working relationships with staff, facility stakeholders, and facility users
* Direct and monitor the work of contractors, engineers, and architects on building projects
* Maintain a hazardous materials communication program and material safety data sheets; maintain knowledge of changes in pertinent federal, state, and local regulations
* All other duties as assigned by the General Manager

Qualifications:

* B.S. or B.A. degree from an accredited college/university is preferred.
* 5-7 years’ experience in facility operations management.
* Must show demonstrated knowledge of physical plant management, supervisory skills, and experience in work crew supervision in facility operations.
* Ability to work event nights, weekends, and holidays as required.
* Knowledge of budget preparation and control.
* Knowledge of OSHA requirements.
* Basic knowledge of boilers, chillers, refrigeration, and ice making.
* Basic Knowledge of Fire Alarms / Fire Protection Systems.
* Knowledge of event production and theater technology.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and Outlook.
* Ability to communicate with employees, co-workers, volunteers, management staff, and guests in a clear, businesslike, and respectful manner, which focuses on generating a positive, enthusiastic, and cooperative work environment.
* Ability to work well in a team-oriented, fast-paced, event-driven environment.
* Working knowledge of equipment safety, facility maintenance, and housekeeping.
* Excellent customer service skills.

Strengthened by our Differences. United to Make a Difference:

At OVG, we understand that to continue positively disrupting the sports and live entertainment industry, we need a diverse team to help us do it. We also believe that inclusivity drives innovation, strengthens our **people**, improves our **service**, and raises our **excellence**. Our success is rooted in creating environments that reflect and celebrate the diverse communities in which we operate and serve, and this is the reason we are committed to amplifying voices from all different backgrounds.

existing_roles.description:
Penn Aluminum International LLC

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

**Location:** Murphysboro, IL (On-Site)

**Who We Are**

Penn Aluminum is part of The Marmon Group, a Berkshire Hathaway Company. The Marmon Group comprises four autonomous companies consisting of 15 diverse, stand-alone business sectors and more than 185 independent manufacturing and service businesses. These businesses operate more than 350 manufacturing, distribution and service facilities, and employ more than 20,000 people worldwide.

Penn Aluminum is a premier manufacturer of aluminum drawn tubing and extruded shapes, providing high quality, engineered solutions to our customers. With strategically located production facilities, we are well positioned to support our customers throughout North America and beyond.

We are seeking a results-driven Director of Operations to lead our aluminum extrusion operations in Murphysboro, IL and Harlingen, TX. Our plants produce precision extruded and drawn tubing and custom profiles for Transportation, HVAC, Electrical, and Consumer Durables markets. Penn is investing over $60M in a state-of-the-art Murphysboro extrusion line that will double our tonnage output and open new markets, and this leader will be central to its success. The ideal candidate combines strong leadership, extrusion expertise, and a proven record of sustaining lean manufacturing across multiple sites.

**What You’ll Do**

* Team Leadership: Develop production managers, supervisors, and front-line employees at both sites, fostering an engaged, collaborative culture.
* Safety & Quality: Champion an uncompromising safety culture, ensure regulatory compliance, and maintain ISO and IATF quality systems and customer satisfaction.
* Multi-Site Operational Leadership: Provide strategic direction and oversight for safe, efficient, cost-effective production at Murphysboro and Harlingen, aligning standards, best practices, and performance metrics across both sites.
* Production Management: Oversee Murphysboro’s four extrusion presses, drawn benches, coil draw lines, cut-to-length, and fabrication, and Harlingen’s 2750T press with draw and heat treat processes.
* Lean & Continuous Improvement: Deploy and sustain lean methodologies (Kaizen, 5S, Value Stream Mapping, Six Sigma) to drive operational excellence.
* Strategic Planning: Partner with the President and executive team on long-term strategy, multi-site capacity planning, capital justification, and budget control.
* Resource Management: Optimize labor, materials, and equipment across both sites to maximize throughput, minimize waste, and improve OEE.
* Expansion Leadership: Lead the commissioning and ramp-up of the new $60M+ Murphysboro extrusion line, preparing people, processes, and supply chain to double tonnage output and grow in new markets

**What You’ll Need**

* Experience: 10+ years of progressive operations management, including at least five in aluminum extrusion; multi-site experience strongly preferred.
* Leadership: Proven ability to manage complex operations and large teams across multiple locations.
* Technical Expertise: Strong knowledge of aluminum metallurgy, extrusion, and downstream operations (drawing, heat treating, cutting, fabrication).
* Lean Acumen: Extensive experience implementing and sustaining lean and continuous improvement. Six Sigma Green Belt strongly preferred.
* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, or a related field preferred.
* Communication: Excellent communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills.
* Travel: Regular travel between Murphysboro and Harlingen.

**What You’ll Gain**

* Competitive salaried compensation
* Comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision, and prescription coverage)
* 401(k) with company matching
* Leadership development and career growth opportunities
* The ability to make a direct impact on safety, customer satisfaction, and operational performance
* A collaborative, results-driven work environment

Pay Range:

132,800.00 - 199,200.00

We offer a comprehensive benefits package that may include medical, dental, vision, 401k matching, and more!

Following receipt of a conditional offer of employment, candidates will be required to complete additional job-related screening processes as permitted or required by applicable law.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all applicants will be considered for employment without attention to their membership in any protected class. If you require any reasonable accommodation to complete your application or any part of the recruiting process, please email your request to careers@marmon.com, and please be sure to include the title and the location of the position for which you are applying.

existing_roles.title: Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology
existing_roles.description:
**Experiencing together a unique human adventure**

Animal health is key to the health of the planet. Working at Virbac means taking part in a unique human adventure in which the engagement of each individual contributes to its evolution. Encouraging internal mobility between positions and countries, offering individual development plans and building a partnership based on trust between managers and employees are as many perspectives of motivation for our teams. We also offer them a work environment conducive to exploring new territories and balancing their professional and personal lives. Finally, fostering their engagement to animal health also means listening to them and helping them to acquire new skills, preparing them for the challenges of tomorrow and encouraging them to contribute to an ever more responsible approach to our business.

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

Virbac Animal Health is seeking a Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology to join our Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) team. The Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology develops, implements, maintains, and improves robust manufacturing processes and facility infrastructure for right-first-time manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs. To plan, schedule, organize, and manage Technology Transfer Projects, CAPEX Engineering Projects, Validation, Technical Support, Alternate Raw Materials, Packaging, Life Cycle Management, and Team Leadership.

**Qualified candidates should possess the following:**

* 8 to 12+ years of Progressively responsible experience in engineering, and production management with a cGMP/FDA-regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Demonstrated track record in CAPEX project management, facility/process design, and multi-team operational leadership across multi-site or regional organizations.
* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.
* Strong multi-team leadership, communication, and cross-functional stakeholder management abilities.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the budget, planning, and robust manufacturing (RFT for the first commercial batches) of technology transfer projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Accountable for the definition and execution of the site and regional project roadmap in alignment with business needs and capability.
* Contributes to the selection of the right technology or CMO, taking into account product needs.
* Establish robust cost estimates (CAPEX, resources, future running costs) and planning estimates to support reliable NPVs and commercial strategy.
* Leadership of scale-up batches, engineering batches, and transfer to production.
* Develops manufacturing documentation (Master Batch Records, Submission batch protocols, etc.).
* Reviews and approves transfer and submission files.

**Expected results:** Ensure the robustness and capability of the process transferred to Manufacturing

**Area of responsibility 2: CAPEX Engineering Projects**

**Main activities:**

* Support and lead CAPEX engineering projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Evaluate, scope, and implement CAPEX projects for facility infrastructure, process improvements, and product needs.
* Responsible for managing annual capital budgets and operating expenses for the department.
* Partner closely with key local and global stakeholders (Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, Finance, etc.) to align project execution with regional operational goals.
* Ensure all engineering projects are performed in full compliance with applicable cGMP standards, EHS regulations, and company sustainability objectives.
* Oversee project budgets, engineering designs, contractor selection, and commissioning/qualification timelines.

**Expected Results:** Successful, on-time, and on-budget delivery of facility, process, and product CAPEX engineering projects that enhance regional capacity, EHS standards, compliance, and efficiency.

**Area of responsibility 3:** Process Improvement & Life Cycle Management (LCM)

**Main Activities:**

* Incorporate structured process improvement concepts (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) across existing product portfolios.
* Lead Life Cycle Management changes to maintain and optimize the existing commercial product portfolio across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Collaborate closely with global and local stakeholders, including Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, and Finance, to evaluate and execute LCM initiatives.

**Expected Results:** Drive continuous product and process enhancement, lower operational costs, ensure ongoing regulatory compliance, and extend product life cycles.

**Area of responsibility 4: Validation**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the generation, technical review, execution, and technical approval of validation deliverables (Validation Master Plan, URS, equipment qualification, process validation, cleaning validation, computer system validation)across NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Lead validation projects and teams
* Ensures risk analysis methods are applied to validation activities
* Follow industry and regulatory trends and expectations (GMP, EHS, and sustainability guidelines).
* Review SOPs and batch documentation to ensure adequacy with validation criteria.
* Ensure prompt deviation resolution, including root cause analysis when required.

**Expected results:** A thorough understanding of the validation status of the regional sites, products, and equipment, with proactive remediation plans addressing any gaps.

**Area of responsibility 5: Technical support.**

**Main activities:**

* Troubleshooting and improvement proposal of current commercial products processes (robustness, productivity, cost efficiency & compliance)
* Lean and methodological approach during trouble shooting of complex product/process deviations
* Take ownership of complex product deviation / CAPA until approval

### **Senior Manager, Operational Excellence - Factor US**

***This role is hybrid to our Goodyear, AZ Factor facility***

### **Company Overview**

At Factor, we are on a mission to revolutionize the way people eat by making healthy, fresh, chef-prepared meals accessible and effortless. As the market leader in the Ready-To-Eat (RTE) meal space, we eliminate the need for cooking and meal prep while delivering high-quality, nutrition-focused meals directly to millions of customers. The Factor team is diverse, high-performing, and fast-growing, offering an inspiring environment where process innovation, operational discipline, and continuous improvement thrive.

### **About the role**

The **Senior Manager, Operational Excellence** leads OpEx capability and multi-site improvement programs across Factor's US ready-to-eat fulfillment, production and distribution network. The role owns projects end to end, from charter and business case through delivery and post-mortem. It combines Lean and Six Sigma methods with senior project-management discipline.

You will serve as a lead advocate for operational transformation by partnering with and challenging business leaders to adopt systems thinking and continuous process innovation.

### **You will...**

* Lead strategic Factor operations projects in continuous improvement, change management, cost optimization and OpEx training across RTE fulfillment networks.
* Direct complex, cross-facility improvement programs, coordinating site leadership with central project teams.
* Own project governance end to end: find high-ROI opportunities, write financially justified charters and capital project justifications, negotiate resources, launch teams, track results and remove roadblocks.
* Deliver projects to demanding schedules and aggressive cost targets, often with changing requirements. Routinely assess project risks and identify alternative paths to offset them.
* Lead the cross-functional project prioritization workflow and scoping program, and facilitate the project pipeline for all stakeholders.
* Develop, improve and maintain the project management process for the organization, and ensure best practices are followed.
* Build organized project plans from complex inputs, track status across a large program, and keep accurate records through frequent iterations.
* Identify new technologies that can deliver meaningful benefits, and champion changes that drive measurable operational improvements.
* Oversee material handling equipment, automation and warehouse projects. Serve as liaison between vendors and site maintenance, operations and technology teams.
* Apply DMAIC, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping and 5-Why to eliminate root causes of operational friction.
* Lead change management and risk mitigation for key operational shifts.
* Capture and scale best practices across production and fulfillment sites.
* Mentor junior project managers, Lean practitioners and floor supervisors in complex system integrations, and provide leadership to assigned teams so key competencies are developed and maintained.
* Support COGS reporting and tool creation. Data-driven, sound bridges, and coordinate actions that reduce COGS.

### **You are...**

* **Strategic leadership:** Influences without direct authority and aligns multi-site leaders around shared operational goals.
* **Project and time management:** Delivers multi-phase process and infrastructure projects on time and within budget.
* **Organization:** Builds organized project plans from complex inputs and keeps accurate records across frequent iterations.
* **Enterprising and creative:** Starts new operational and strategic projects, and challenges conventional methods with new ideas.
* **Cross-functional collaboration**: Bridges Central Strategy, Food Safety & Quality Assurance, Logistics, Procurement and DC Operations.
* **Stakeholder facilitation:** Negotiates, facilitates and resolves conflicting priorities across local and central stakeholders.
* **Communication:** Independently manages the cadence of formal and informal communication across all levels of the organization.
* **Critical thinking:** Weighs the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions before committing.
* **Data-driven**: Interprets operational telemetry, unit economics and process-flow metrics to make decisions.
* **Coaching and mentorship:** Coaches floor supervisors, Lean practitioners and project managers with constructive, empathy-driven feedback.
* **Driven by results**: Pushes projects to completion with urgency, focused on tangible business outcomes.

### **You have...**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, or equivalent management experience.
* 7+ years of experience in continuous improvement / OpEx roles within food manufacturing, RTE operations, or cold-chain logistics.
* Has led cross-facility or multi-site improvement programs.
* Hands-on use of DMAIC, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping and 5-Why.
* Master Black Belt or PMP Certification preferred.
* Extensive experience with Google Workspace.
* Experience with project management software.
* Experience utilizing AI tools and workflows.

### **Travel...**

* Travel: 25%-50% across Factor's national US fulfillment and production network

### **You'll get...**

* Competitive salary, 401k with company match that vests immediately upon participation
* Generous PTO, including sabbatical, and parental leave of up to 16 weeks
* Comprehensive health and wellness benefits with options at $0 monthly, effective first day of employment
* Tuition reimbursement for continuing education (upon 2 years of service)
* Up to 85% discount on subscriptions to HelloFresh meal plans (HelloFresh, Green Chef, Everyplate, and Factor\_)
* Access to Employee Resource Groups that are open to all employees, including those pertaining to BIPOC, women, veterans, parents, and LGBTQ+
* Inclusive, collaborative, and dynamic work environment within a fast-paced, mission-driven company that is disrupting the traditional food supply chain

This job description is intended to provide a general overview of the responsibilities. However, the Company reserves the right to adjust, modify, or reassign work tasks and responsibilities as needed to meet changing business needs, operational requirements, or other factors.

**Director, Fund Operations**

**POSITION:** Full-time Exempt

**DEPARTMENT:** Impact Investing

**REPORTS TO:** Vice President, Impact Investing

**About the Organization**

**A FOUNDATION BUILT ON GREATER ATLANTA’S FUTURE**

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta is one of the nation’s largest community foundations, with over $1.7 billion in assets and more than seven decades of philanthropic leadership. Through grants, donor services, civic partnerships and impact investments, CFGA advances equity and opportunity across 23 counties in the Greater Atlanta region.

**The Role**

**BUILDING THE OPERATING FOUNDATION FOR IMPACT INVESTING**

The Director of Fund Operations will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s impact investing fund platform. This role is responsible for strengthening and scaling the systems, processes, infrastructure, and controls necessary to support a growing and sophisticated investment portfolio. This person owns the end-to-end operating model for the Foundation's impact investment platform. This is a senior, hands-on role responsible for making sure that once an investment is approved, it closes, funds, is serviced and is reported on correctly, on time and with a clear record. The work spans closing, funding, servicing, fund administration, compliance, records, data and reporting. This role supports every fund and vehicle on the platform — including the GoATL Community Capacity Fund, GoATL Affordable Housing Fund, TogetherATL Affordable Housing Fund, GoATL Community Guarantee Pool, and the Atlanta Affordable Housing Fund — together with related joint ventures and special purpose entities.

In practice, this person is the platform’s operational backbone: the person who knows what each transaction and fund requires, organizes the people and documents needed to satisfy those requirements, maintains the authoritative record, anticipates deadlines and exceptions, and follows issues through to resolution. The Director does not practice law or make accounting or credit decisions. Instead, the role makes sure Legal, Finance and the investment team work together smoothly and that nothing falls through the cracks.

The Director works hand in hand with the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing, who sits in Finance. The Director owns the process and the operating record: deadlines, checklists, documents, vendor performance and the loan database. The Fund Accountant owns the books: the general ledger, fund financial statements, capital accounts, investor statements and audit work. The Director makes sure the right information arrives complete and on time; the Fund Accountant decides how it is recorded and signs off on the numbers.

The successful candidate will combine transaction discipline, financial fluency, legal-document literacy, systems thinking and persistent follow-through. This person must be comfortable moving between a closing checklist, a fund agreement, a late borrower report, a wire request, a reporting calendar and a vendor escalation without losing track of what the governing documents require or the record of what was done.

**Why This Role Matters**

The platform now manages more than 60 loans across multiple funds and vehicles and is preparing to deploy its next round of capital. It has outgrown a model in which staff fill each operational gap as it appears. This role will connect the investment team, Finance, Legal and outside providers into one way of working: smooth closings, consistent records, clear deadlines, and systems that hold what we know about each fund, relationship and investment, so that knowledge does not live only in people’s heads.

* Creates one accountable owner for the transaction and fund lifecycle after investment approval.
* Replaces informal handoffs and institutional memory with documented workflows, complete records, calendars, controls and escalation paths.
* Gives Finance (including the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing), Legal and Portfolio Management a disciplined operating counterpart while preserving their independent authority.
* Ensures outside administrators, servicers and specialists work as extensions of our own process, with the Foundation keeping ownership of its records and decisions.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

**Transaction Closing and Funding Coordination**

* Own the closing process from approval through funding and loan setup with the servicer, maintaining a complete checklist of approval conditions, legal documents, due diligence, signatures, funding mechanics and post-closing items. Because real estate deals fund on the day of closing, every item, including the wire request, must be ready before signing day.
* Translate investment approvals and term sheets into coordinated workplans for the deal lead, Legal, Finance and the Fund Accountant, Treasury, the borrower and outside providers; surface conflicts, gaps and sequencing issues early.
* Coordinate document production and review, signature processes, lien and lender-agreement requirements, organizational documents, insurance, required consents and other closing deliverables. Track legal questions to formal resolution by counsel.
* Confirm that every funding and wire request is complete before it goes to Finance or Treasury: required approvals are in place, the borrower’s wire instructions have been verified by a phone call, and two people are involved in every wire. Maintain the standard wire request form used for both closings and construction draws.
* Ensure each closed transaction is set up accurately and handed off to the assigned portfolio owner with final documents, payment terms, covenants, reporting obligations, draw requirements and key dates recorded in the system of record under the loan’s ID.
* Give the Fund Accountant the final executed terms, funded amounts and key dates for each closing, so the loan is set up in the books from the same record.

**Fund and Entity Operations**

* Manage operating calendars and workflows for each fund, entity and capital source, including capital calls, distributions, investor onboarding, bank account administration (account openings and authorized signers), subscriptions, side letters, governance actions and record retention. The Fund Accountant calculates investor allocations, capital accounts and distribution amounts and records them; this role runs the calendar, notices and documents around them.
* Own a single, current investor contact list, including financial advisors and fund administrator portal access, so that capital call notices, reports and distributions reach the right people.
* Maintain one register of what each fund is required to do under its governing agreements, side letters, policies, approval authorities and committee actions; coordinate implementation with the accountable business, Legal and Finance owners.
* Track state filings, annual report deadlines and registered-agent requirements across all entities, and support General Counsel as needed in preparing and completing these filings. General Counsel owns legal and state filings and Finance owns tax and regulatory filings; this role keeps one shared calendar for all of them.
* Support cash forecasting and liquidity planning by giving the Fund Accountant and the Vice President, Impact Investing expected closing, draw and repayment dates, while preserving Finance's authority over cash, treasury policy and accounting treatment.
* Support Finance-led annual audits and tax work by gathering key information and answering common requests. The Fund Accountant manages the audit and the auditor relationship, and Finance keeps ownership of audit and tax strategy, filings and sign-off. Organize valuations and other fund-level deliverables by assembling source materials, tracking deadlines, coordinating responses and driving open items to resolution.

**Servicing and Portfolio Operations**

* Own the operational relationship with loan servicers and administrators, including billing, payment processing, notices, escrows, statements, payoff calculations, deadline reminders and follow-up on exceptions.
* Ensure payments, draws, amendments, waivers, modifications and payoff activity are documented, routed and recorded consistently. Escalate issues that stay unresolved and any service failures.
* Run the quarterly borrower reporting process: track whether each report has arrived and is complete, send notices when reports are late or missing pieces, and make sure reviewed figures are recorded in the system of record.
* Keep the calendar for annual affordability compliance reviews (rents, incomes and other terms required by each loan’s affordability restrictions) and loan maturities, so reviews by asset managers happen on schedule.
* Coordinate operational support for loans in workout or needing special attention, including document collection, approval tracking, counsel coordination and implementation of authorized actions.
* Distinguish operational monitoring from credit judgment: route substantive covenant, borrower-performance and risk matters to Portfolio and Asset Management and track resulting actions to completion.

**Data, Records and Reporting Infrastructure**

* Carry out the platform’s plan to move from scattered files and systems (including Foundant, SharePoint, Excel, the DocuSign data room, and the fund administrator’s Egnyte and Salesforce portal) to a single system of record, working with Investment, Finance, Legal, IT and the fund administrator.
* In coordination with IT and third-party partners, establish and maintain the system of record (a loan database) for fund, investor and transaction information, with clear ownership, access controls, shared IDs, naming standards and a full history of changes. Key terms lock at closing and change only through a dated, approved modification.
* Work with IT to build and maintain automated workflows (for example, in Power Automate) that move data between systems, send deadline alerts and refresh Power BI dashboards, and use AI tools to prepare summaries and checks for staff to review. Coordinate with the Fund Accountant so the loan database and the accounting records tie out.
* Own operational data quality and check that key fields match across closing records, servicing systems, administrator records and Finance systems; resolve any differences with the appropriate source owner.
* Maintain the master calendar for investor reporting, committee, board, audit, tax, compliance and portfolio deliverables and coordinate timely inputs from accountable content owners.

**Vendor Management and Process Improvement**

* Serve as the primary business owner for third-party fund administration, servicing, payment processing and related operational providers; set service standards, make sure the Foundation has access to the source records, and define how issues are escalated and when a provider can be replaced.
* Share vendor oversight with the Fund Accountant: this role owns the relationship, contract terms, service standards and timeliness; the Fund Accountant reviews the financial accuracy of what providers produce (interest, balances, investor statements and fund reports) before it is posted or shared.
* Monitor service performance, check that provider reports arrive on time and match the operating record (the Fund Accountant checks the financial figures) and lead resolution of errors, backlogs and control failures.
* Document and continuously improve workflows for approvals, closings, disbursements, servicing, amendments, reporting and record retention. Partner with the Fund Accountant where workflows touch the books, such as the monthly close; Finance owns accounting procedures and reconciliations.
* Design procedures that are durable, teachable and appropriately scaled rather than dependent on one employee's memory or heroics.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

* Manage any future operations or servicing staff; establish clear ownership, service expectations and backup coverage.
* Run recurring operating meetings that convert cross-functional issues into decisions, named owners and deadlines.
* Refine roles, responsibilities, workflows, and accountability standards across teams involved in fund operations and investment management.
* Raise issues promptly and concisely with the Vice President, Impact Investing and enterprise leadership (legal and finance) when service failures, unresolved legal or financial questions, capacity constraints or control gaps threaten a closing, obligation or relationship.
* Build strong working relationships across teams while being willing to insist on complete documentation, clear authority and timely decisions.

**Qualifications**  
**WHAT YOU BRING**

**Required**

* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in fund operations, transaction management, loan administration, investment operations, structured finance, real estate finance, private credit, community development finance or a closely related field.
* Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, real estate, public administration or a related field required.
* Demonstrated experience coordinating transactions through closing and funding, including legal documentation, cash mechanics and post-closing requirements.
* Working knowledge of financial statements, loan and investment documents, entity and fund records, payment and servicing processes, reconciliations and internal controls.
* Ability to build, lead, and evolve operational functions within a growing or complex organization.
* Confidence in evaluating existing practices, constructively challenging the status quo, and driving meaningful process improvements.
* Exceptional project management and organizational judgment, with the ability to maintain accuracy across multiple vehicles, transactions, deadlines and stakeholders.
* Strong written communication and the ability to convert complex requirements into clear checklists, procedures, records and short, clear updates for leadership when something is off track.
* Experience holding internal and external partners accountable, escalating appropriately and following issues through closure.
* A clear commitment to CFGA’s mission of equity and shared prosperity for all.

**Preferred**

* Experience with affordable housing, community development lending, program-related investments, impact investing or philanthropic investment vehicles.
* Experience managing a third-party fund administrator, loan servicer, closing counsel, tax provider or comparable outsourced operating partner.
* Experience building or improving an operating model, system of record, compliance calendar or reporting infrastructure.
* Comfort with Microsoft 365 tools such as SharePoint, Lists, Power Automate and Power BI; loan or relationship management systems such as Foundant or Salesforce; and tools used to summarize and check documents.
* Masters degree in relevant field.
* Relevant legal-operations, paralegal, fund-administration or project-management training is valuable; a law degree or CPA is not required.

**HYBRID SCHEDULE**

The Community Foundation operates in a hybrid working environment with staff working in-office three days per week and the opportunity to work two days remotely per week if in good standing.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications. The salary range is

$130,000 - $150,000. This position is exempt and eligible for the Foundation’s competitive health and benefits plan, which includes:

**Paid time off**

* Four weeks accrued paid vacation
* Two weeks accrued paid sick leave
* Four mental health days
* Two personal days
* Two floating holidays
* Ten holidays

**Benefits**

* All benefits effective on date of hire with no waiting period
* 100% employer-paid medical, dental and vision coverage for employee-only plans
* 100% employer-paid life insurance, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability
* 100% employer-paid downtown Atlanta parking or monthly MARTA card
* Affordable plans for legal insurance, critical illness, supplemental life and more
* Immediate eligibility to contribute to a 403(b), plus a 6% employer-paid contribution after one year regardless of employee contributions
* Cell phone stipend
* Employee Donor Advised Fund after one year
* Employee Assistance Program and more

**Culture, Learning & Development**

* Individual Development Plans with training, resources and development opportunities
* Two wellness rooms with self-care resources
* Monthly employee engagement activities

**TO APPLY**

Submit your resume and cover letter through our Careers website.

Note: Only applications submitted through our website will be accepted. Due to the volume of candidates, we are unable to provide status updates or accommodate phone calls or walk-ins regarding open positions.

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta values diversity and inclusion; we honor the diverse needs, strengths, voices and backgrounds of all individuals in our regional community.

At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
  
  
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
  
  
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
  
  
Let’s Get Loco!
  
  
What’s in it for you!
  
  

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:**  
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for driving El Pollo Loco’s success in the Los Angeles, CA region. They are responsible for providing operational expertise, strategic leadership and coaching. Directs, leads, manages and analyzes all aspects of the restaurant operations for the Areas under their direction to ensure achievement and maintenance of the regional sales, budgetary targets, controllable profit, performance metrics (e.g., service, quality, cleanliness, etc.), brand integrity, and compliance standards (e.g., food and restaurant safety, federal/state/local labor laws, etc.). Implements and executes strategic and tactical operational initiatives that support future business growth strategies. Oversees and manages adequate resource availability for existing and new restaurant openings including the attraction, retention, training, development and coaching of a high performing management team.
  
  
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* Oversees all aspects of the region’s restaurant business, operations, and facilities. Directs and aligns company strategies with restaurant management activities.
* Utilizes reporting systems to determine trends in sales, cost of goods and guest services. Reviews, monitors and manages the financial progress of the individual restaurants and region, including food and labor costs, ensuring budgeted targets are achieved.
* Meets regularly with Area Leaders to coach, develop, train and review performance, share best practices and disseminate information on any areas where there is an opportunity for improvement (e.g., P&L, RCP, FSA, QSC, Mystery Shops, etc.). Develops action plans with Area Leaders to improve revenue, profitability and quality/service standards.
* Directs, manages and ensures the region’s successful and timely implementation of all marketing strategies and LTOs. Supports and inspects marketing strategies in building guest counts and sales.
* Provides effective and timely resolution to all guest and employee complaints, conflicts and employee relations that cannot be resolved at the Area Leader level.
* Ensures the region’s restaurants are in compliance with all local, regional, and national laws and have all the required documentation and paperwork.
* Leverages two-way communication with Field and Support Center employees. Represents the Operations perspective on prioritization, planning and promotions to inspire operational excellence, effective implementation and facilitate insights. Provides specific operational input and feedback into the development of new products and programs to ensure successful execution.
* Collaborates with Development, Human Resources, and Operations in the coordination and execution of new restaurant openings. Directs team selection, monitors the training and ensures the teams perform to El Pollo Loco’s standards. Participates in the local public relations support in all locations. Approves employee relocation within region ensuring moves are conducted in the most economical and efficient manner.
* Develops regional succession plans: evaluates open opportunities, assesses internal talent, oversees management training programs, and drives recruiting efforts to ensure adequate number of managers are available to sustain growth of the organization.
* Champions effective vertical and horizontal communications within the regional area including Company-wide news of interest, upcoming events, new facilities, promotions, product developments, “Best Practices” among peers, etc. Prepares thoroughly and delivers well-organized, dynamic and informative presentations to senior management as needed. Holds meetings with their respective teams on a regular basis to ensure fluid and consistent messaging.
* Creates and fosters a positive team environment through recognizing and reinforcing behaviors and results that are aligned with El Pollo Loco’s core values and culture. Ensures open channels for employee suggestions.
* Interacts professionally and ethically, constructively participating as a collaborative team leader in pursuit of common goals, including active attendance to meetings. Initiates cost-effective suggestions to improve operational procedures.
* Other activities, duties or responsibilities that are assigned by your supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
  
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
  
  
**Education/Work Experience:**  
High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required, BA/BS degree in Business Administration preferred. 8+ years QSR/multi-site restaurant experience as an Area Leader or District Manager required; 5+ years regional QSR management experience preferred; 3+ years El Pollo Loco experience preferred; and a track record of success in leading, managing, coaching and developing high performance teams.
  
  
**License/Certifications:**  
Current valid driver’s license required as frequent weekly travel is involved. Current ServSafe certification preferred.
  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  

* Experience with successfully recruiting, building, and developing a team (based on current and future needs).
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives.
* Must be decisive and able to make fact-based decisions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners.
* Ability to prioritize and plan work assignments and work under pressure of frequent and tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex reports, documents, and correspondence.
* Adept at managing and prioritizing competing time sensitive requests while working well in a team atmosphere that may be under pressure.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significance to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Must be willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state restaurant locations, as needed by car or airplane.

Our Company
  
  
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. And today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide customers with fresh and innovative L.A. Mex from our famous family dinners to Mexican entrees.
  
  
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. Individual pay will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.
